A2 — enumeration (safe, read-only):

python
def check_enumeration(ctx):
    out = []
    # find login form
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return out
    known_email = ctx.args.test_email or f"wp-user-{rand_token('', 6)}@example.test"
    random_email = f"wp-{rand_token('', 8)}@wpexampletest"
    
    def try_login(email, password):
        data = {}
        for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
            if re.search(r"(?i)user|email|login|identifier", k):
                data[k] = email
            elif re.search(r"(?i)pass|pwd|password", k):
                data[k] = password
            else:
                data[k] = v
        # refresh csrf
        ...
        return ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=False)
    
    known = try_login(ctx.args.test_email, "wrongpw" + rand_token("", 6))
    random_ = try_login(random_email, "wrongpw" + rand_token("", 6))
    
    if known is None or random_ is None:
        return out
    
    # Compare
    if known.status != random_.status or \
       similar(known.text, random_.text) < 0.85 or \
       abs(known.elapsed - random_.elapsed) > 0.5:
        out.append(Finding("enum", "medium", "Username/email enumeration via login",
                          f["action"], method="POST",
                          evidence=f"known: HTTP {known.status}, {len(known.body)}B, "
                                   f"{known.elapsed*1000:.0f}ms; "
                                   f"random: HTTP {random_.status}, {len(random_.body)}B, "
                                   f"{random_.elapsed*1000:.0f}ms",
                          remediation="Use identical responses and constant-time comparison "
                                      "for known vs unknown accounts.",
                          phase=2))
    return out
A3 — brute force (bounded):

python
def check_bruteforce(ctx):
    out = []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f or not ctx.args.test_email:
        return out
    attempts = min(ctx.args.rate_count, 20)
    statuses = []
    for i in range(attempts):
        data = {}
        for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
            if re.search(r"(?i)user|email|login", k):
                data[k] = ctx.args.test_email
            elif re.search(r"(?i)pass|pwd", k):
                data[k] = f"wrongpw{rand_token('', 6)}"
            else:
                data[k] = v
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=False)
        if r:
            statuses.append(r.status)
    limited = any(s in (429, 403, 503) for s in statuses)
    if not limited and len(statuses) == attempts:
        out.append(Finding("bruteforce", "medium", "No rate limiting on login endpoint",
                          f["action"], method="POST",
                          evidence=f"{len(statuses)} failed attempts without 429/lockout; "
                                   f"statuses={sorted(set(statuses))}",
                          remediation="Add per-account and per-IP rate limiting with "
                                      "exponential backoff.",
                          phase=2))
    return out
A5 — default creds:

python
DEFAULT_CREDS = [("admin", "admin"), ("admin", "password"), ("admin", "admin123"),
                 ("admin", "123456"), ("admin", "letmein"), ("administrator", "admin"),
                 ("root", "root"), ("root", "toor"), ("test", "test")]

def check_default_creds(ctx):
    out = []
    if not ctx.args.admin_login:
        return out
    url = ctx.args.admin_login
    for user, pw in DEFAULT_CREDS:
        data = {"username": user, "password": pw, "email": user, "login": user}
        r = ctx.http.fetch(url, "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status >= 400:
            continue
        if not re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|error|denied)", r.text[:3000]):
            out.append(Finding("default-creds", "critical", "Default admin credentials accepted",
                              url, method="POST", payload=f"{user}:{pw}",
                              evidence=f"HTTP {r.status} with no rejection markers, "
                                       f"final URL: {r.url}",
                              remediation="Remove default accounts immediately; enforce MFA on "
                                          "admin login.",
                              confidence="medium", phase=2))
            break
    return out
B1 — reset token:

python
def check_reset_token(ctx):
    out = []
    # find reset form
    reset_form = None
    for page in ctx.pages:
        if not re.search(r"(?i)forgot|reset|recover", page["url"]):
            continue
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if f["method"] == "POST" and any(re.search(r"(?i)email|user", k) for k in f["inputs"]):
                reset_form = (page["url"], f)
                break
        if reset_form:
            break
    if not reset_form or not ctx.args.test_email:
        return out
    
    page_url, f = reset_form
    tokens = []
    for _ in range(2):
        data = {}
        for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
            if re.search(r"(?i)email|user|login", k):
                data[k] = ctx.args.test_email
            else:
                data[k] = v
        # refresh csrf
        ...
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        # Look for token in response (sometimes leaked) or URL
        m = re.search(r"[?&](?:token|t|code|key)=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{16,})", r.url)
        if m:
            tokens.append(m.group(1))
        # Or in body
        m = re.search(r"(?:token|t|code|key)[\"'=:\s]+([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{16,})", r.text)
        if m:
            tokens.append(m.group(1))
    
    if len(tokens) >= 2:
        if tokens[0] == tokens[1]:
            out.append(Finding("reset", "high", "Reset token is static/reused",
                              f["action"], method="POST",
                              evidence=f"identical token on consecutive requests: "
                                       f"{tokens[0][:8]}...",
                              remediation="Generate a fresh CSPRNG token per request; "
                                          "invalidate after use and after expiry.",
                              phase=2))
        else:
            t = tokens[0]
            if len(t) < 16 or shannon(t) < 3.5:
                out.append(Finding("reset", "medium", "Low-entropy reset token",
                                  f["action"], method="POST",
                                  evidence=f"length={len(t)}, entropy={shannon(t):.2f}",
                                  remediation="Use at least 128 bits of entropy; base64url-encode.",
                                  phase=2))
    return out
B2 — host header injection:

python
def check_host_header_reset(ctx):
    out = []
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return out
    # find reset form
    reset_form = None
    for page in ctx.pages:
        if not re.search(r"(?i)forgot|reset|recover", page["url"]):
            continue
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if f["method"] == "POST" and any(re.search(r"(?i)email|user", k) for k in f["inputs"]):
                reset_form = (page["url"], f)
                break
        if reset_form:
            break
    if not reset_form:
        return out
    page_url, f = reset_form
    
    for header, val in [("Host", "evil-wp.example"), ("X-Forwarded-Host", "evil-wp.example")]:
        data = {}
        for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
            if re.search(r"(?i)email|user|login", k):
                data[k] = ctx.args.test_email
            else:
                data[k] = v
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data),
                          headers={header: val}, follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if "evil-wp.example" in r.text or "evil-wp.example" in r.url:
            out.append(Finding("reset-host", "high",
                              f"Host header injection in password reset ({header})",
                              f["action"], method="POST", payload=f"{header}: {val}",
                              evidence="attacker-controlled host reflected in reset flow",
                              remediation="Hard-code the canonical base URL for password "
                                          "reset links; ignore Host/X-Forwarded-Host.",
                              phase=2))
    return out
C2 — session fixation:

python
def check_session_fixation(ctx):
    out = []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f or not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return out
    
    # Fresh session — capture pre-auth cookies
    fresh = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    pre = fresh.fetch(page_url, follow=True)
    pre_cookies = {}
    for c in fresh.jar:
        pre_cookies[c.name] = c.value
    
    # Login
    data = {}
    for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
        if re.search(r"(?i)user|email|login", k):
            data[k] = ctx.args.test_email
        elif re.search(r"(?i)pass|pwd", k):
            data[k] = ctx.args.test_password
        else:
            data[k] = v
    r = fresh.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    post_cookies = {c.name: c.value for c in fresh.jar}
    
    # Compare session cookies
    session_names = set()
    for name in set(pre_cookies) | set(post_cookies):
        if re.search(r"(?i)sess|sid|auth", name):
            session_names.add(name)
    
    for name in session_names:
        pre_val = pre_cookies.get(name)
        post_val = post_cookies.get(name)
        if pre_val and pre_val == post_val:
            out.append(Finding("session-fix", "high", "Session fixation: ID not rotated on login",
                              f["action"], method="POST", param=name,
                              evidence=f"cookie {name} unchanged across authentication",
                              remediation="Issue a fresh session ID on every authentication "
                                          "state change; invalidate the pre-auth ID.",
                              phase=2))
    return out
C4 — logout invalidation:

python
def check_logout_invalidation(ctx):
    out = []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f or not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return out
    
    # Login with fresh jar
    authed = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    data = {}
    for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
        if re.search(r"(?i)user|email|login", k):
            data[k] = ctx.args.test_email
        elif re.search(r"(?i)pass|pwd", k):
            data[k] = ctx.args.test_password
        else:
            data[k] = v
    authed.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=True)
    
    # Find logout link
    logout_url = None
    home = authed.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if home:
        links, _, _ = parse_page(home.text, home.url)
        for l in links:
            if re.search(r"(?i)logout|sign-out|signout", l):
                logout_url = l
                break
    if not logout_url:
        # try common
        for p in ("/logout", "/signout", "/api/logout", "/api/auth/logout"):
            r = authed.fetch(ctx.root + p, follow=True)
            if r and r.status < 400:
                logout_url = ctx.root + p
                break
    
    if not logout_url:
        return out
    
    # Capture session cookie before logout
    pre_logout = {c.name: c.value for c in authed.jar}
    authed.fetch(logout_url, follow=True)
    
    # Try replaying the pre-logout cookie
    replay_jar = "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in pre_logout.items())
    replay = ctx.http.clone(cookie=replay_jar)
    r = replay.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is not None and r.status < 400:
        # Compare against unauthenticated baseline
        anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
        if anon and similar(anon.text, r.text) < 0.9:
            # Looks like the authenticated content is still accessible
            # But could also be a caching issue — check if logout left us authed
            out.append(Finding("logout", "high", "Session not invalidated on logout",
                              logout_url,
                              evidence=f"replay of pre-logout cookie still returns "
                                       f"authenticated-looking content "
                                       f"(HTTP {r.status})",
                              remediation="Invalidate server-side session state on logout; "
                                          "clear cookies with matching Path/Domain.",
                              confidence="medium", phase=2))
    return out
C5 — concurrent sessions:

python
def check_concurrent_sessions(ctx):
    out = []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f or not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return out
    
    def login():
        c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
        data = {}
        for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
            if re.search(r"(?i)user|email|login", k):
                data[k] = ctx.args.test_email
            elif re.search(r"(?i)pass|pwd", k):
                data[k] = ctx.args.test_password
            else:
                data[k] = v
        r = c.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=True)
        return c, r
    
    c1, r1 = login()
    time.sleep(0.5)
    c2, r2 = login()
    time.sleep(0.5)
    
    # Check both sessions still valid
    check1 = c1.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    check2 = c2.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon_text = anon.text if anon else ""
    
    valid1 = check1 and check1.status < 400 and similar(anon_text, check1.text) < 0.9
    valid2 = check2 and check2.status < 400 and similar(anon_text, check2.text) < 0.9
    
    if valid1 and valid2:
        out.append(Finding("session-conc", "info", "Concurrent sessions allowed",
                          f["action"], method="POST",
                          evidence="two independent logins both remain valid",
                          remediation="Confirm this is intended policy; consider notifying "
                                      "users of new sign-ins.",
                          phase=2))
    return out
C6 — remember me:

python
def check_remember_me(ctx):
    out = []
    r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    # Look for persistent cookies (with Max-Age or Expires far out)
    for cookie in r.header_all("Set-Cookie"):
        if not re.search(r"(?i)remember|persistent|stay", cookie):
            continue
        name = cookie.split("=", 1)[0]
        val = cookie.split("=", 1)[1].split(";", 1)[0] if "=" in cookie else ""
        if len(val) < 8 or shannon(val) < 3.0:
            out.append(Finding("remember", "medium", f"Weak 'remember me' token: {name}",
                              r.url, param=name,
                              evidence=f"length={len(val)}, entropy={shannon(val):.2f}",
                              remediation="Use a high-entropy token; rotate on each use; "
                                          "add HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite.",
                              phase=2))
    return out
C7 — token in URL:

def check_token_in_url(ctx):
    out = []
    token_re = re.compile(r"(?i)(?:token|session|sid|auth|jwt)=([A-Za-z0-9_\-.]{20,})")
    for url in ctx.discovered:
        m = token_re.search(url)
        if not m:
            continue
        out.append(Finding("token-in-url", "medium", "Session token in URL",
                          url, param=m.group(0).split("=")[0],
                          evidence=f"token visible in URL query string "
                                   f"(len={len(m.group(1))})",
                          remediation="Never place session tokens in URLs; use cookies "
                                      "or Authorization headers.",
                          phase=2))
    return out
C8 — cache controls:

def check_cache_controls(ctx):
    out = []
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return out
    # login then fetch authed page
    authed = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(authed, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return out
    r = authed.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    cc = r.header("Cache-Control", "").lower()
    has_no_store = "no-store" in cc or "private" in cc
    if not has_no_store:
        out.append(Finding("cache-ctrl", "low", "Authenticated page lacks no-store",
                          r.url,
                          evidence=f"Cache-Control: {cc or '(unset)'}",
                          remediation="Send Cache-Control: no-store on authenticated "
                                      "responses.",
                          phase=2))
    return out
D4 — JWT expiry:

python
def check_jwt_expiry(ctx):
    out = []
    for name, tok in ctx.tokens[:4]:
        dec = decode_jwt(tok)
        if not dec:
            continue
        header, payload, _, _ = dec
        if "exp" not in payload:
            out.append(Finding("jwt", "medium", "JWT has no exp claim", ctx.base_url,
                              param=name,
                              evidence=f"claims: {list(payload.keys())}",
                              remediation="Always include exp and enforce it server-side.",
                              phase=2))
            continue
        exp = payload["exp"]
        now = int(time.time())
        if isinstance(exp, (int, float)) and exp - now > 86400 * 30:
            out.append(Finding("jwt", "low", "JWT expiry is unusually long", ctx.base_url,
                              param=name,
                              evidence=f"exp is {(exp - now) / 86400:.0f} days from now",
                              remediation="Use short-lived access tokens (≤1h) with refresh "
                                          "tokens.",
                              phase=2))
    return out
D5 — JWT PII:

python
PII_CLAIMS = ["email", "phone", "ssn", "address", "dob", "birth", "name", "credit",
              "card", "passport", "national_id", "tax_id", "iban", "account"]
def check_jwt_pii(ctx):
    out = []
    for name, tok in ctx.tokens[:4]:
        dec = decode_jwt(tok)
        if not dec:
            continue
        _, payload, _, _ = dec
        hits = [k for k in payload if any(p.lower() in k.lower() for p in PII_CLAIMS)]
        if hits:
            out.append(Finding("jwt", "medium", "Sensitive data in JWT payload", ctx.base_url,
                              param=name,
                              evidence=f"claims containing potential PII: {', '.join(hits)}",
                              remediation="JWTs are base64-encoded, not encrypted. Move PII "
                                          "out of the token payload.",
                              phase=2))
    return out

def check_authz(ctx):
    out = []
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return out
    # Login as customer
    customer = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(customer, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return out
    # Try admin routes
    admin_paths = ["/admin", "/admin/dashboard", "/admin/users", "/admin/settings",
                   "/api/admin", "/api/v1/admin", "/admin/operations", "/staff", "/manage"]
    for p in admin_paths:
        url = ctx.root + p
        r = customer.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status >= 400:
            continue
        if re.search(r"(?i)(login|sign in|unauthorized|forbidden)", r.text[:2000]):
            continue
        if ADMIN_MARKERS.search(r.text):
            out.append(Finding("authz", "critical",
                              f"Customer can access admin interface: {p}", url,
                              evidence=f"HTTP 200 with admin markers "
                                       f"({clip(r.text[:160], 160)})",
                              remediation="Enforce role checks on every admin route and API.",
                              phase=2))
    return out

For the login helper, I need to make sure the CSRF token refresh works. Let me write auto_login_into to accept a client:

python
def auto_login_into(client, ctx, email, password):
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return False, "no login form found"
    # refresh CSRF
    page = client.fetch(page_url, follow=True)
    params = dict(f["inputs"])
    if page:
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        want = urllib.parse.urlsplit(f["action"]).path
        for g in forms:
            if urllib.parse.urlsplit(g["action"]).path == want:
                for k, v in g["inputs"].items():
                    if re.search(r"(?i)token|csrf|nonce", k):
                        params[k] = v
                break
    for k in params:
        if re.search(r"(?i)user|email|login|identifier", k):
            params[k] = email
        elif re.search(r"(?i)pass|pwd", k):
            params[k] = password
    r = client.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return False, "login request failed"
    if r.status >= 400:
        return False, f"HTTP {r.status}"
    if re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed)", r.text[:3000]):
        return False, "rejected"
    return True, r.url

WEAK_PASSWORDS = ["123456", "password", "abc123", "12345678", "qwerty",
                  "111111", "letmein", "welcome", "admin", "1q2w3e"]

DEFAULT_CREDS = [
    ("admin", "admin"), ("admin", "password"), ("admin", "admin123"),
    ("admin", "123456"), ("admin", "letmein"), ("administrator", "admin"),
    ("administrator", "password"), ("root", "root"), ("root", "toor"),
    ("test", "test"), ("test", "test123"),
]

LOGIN_USER_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(user|email|login|identifier|uname|username)")
LOGIN_PASS_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(pass|pwd|password|passwd)")
CSRF_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)token|csrf|nonce|authenticity|_wpnonce")

RESET_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(forgot|reset|recover|password-reset)")
RESET_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)[?&](?:token|t|code|key)=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{16,})")

SESSION_COOKIE_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(sess|sid|auth|jwt|remember|token|^jsessionid$|"
                               r"^phpsessid$|^laravel_session$|^_rails_session$|"
                               r"^asp\.net_sessionid$|^connect\.sid$)")

              "family_name", "credit", "card", "passport", "national_id",
              "tax_id", "iban", "account", "salary"]

2. Operational controls — add before HttpClient
python
def in_testing_window(window: str) -> bool:
    if not window:
        return True
    m = re.match(r"^\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*-\s*(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*$", window)
    if not m:
        return True
    sh, sm, eh, em = map(int, m.groups())
    cur = time.localtime()
    c = cur.tm_hour * 60 + cur.tm_min
    start, end = sh * 60 + sm, eh * 60 + em
    return start <= c <= end if start <= end else (c >= start or c <= end)


class ActivityLog:
    def __init__(self, path: str):
        self.path = path
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        if path:
            with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write(f"# webprobe {VERSION} session started "
                         f"{time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')}\n")

    def record(self, test_id: str, outcome: str, description: str,
               evidence: str = "") -> None:
        if not self.path:
            return
        line = (f"{time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S')}\t{test_id}\t{outcome}\t"
                f"{description}\t{evidence[:500]}\n")
        with self.lock:
            with open(self.path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write(line)


class InstabilityMonitor:
    def __init__(self, threshold: float = 0.05, min_samples: int = 20):
        self.total = 0
        self.errors = 0
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.min_samples = min_samples
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.aborted = False

    def observe(self, status: int) -> None:
        with self.lock:
            self.total += 1
            if status >= 500:
                self.errors += 1
            if self.total >= self.min_samples and \
                    self.errors / self.total > self.threshold:
                self.aborted = True


_ABORT_CACHE: Dict[str, bool] = {}


def aborted(ctx) -> bool:
    if ctx.args.abort_file:
        mtime = os.path.getmtime(ctx.args.abort_file) if os.path.exists(
            ctx.args.abort_file) else 0
        key = ctx.args.abort_file
        if mtime and _ABORT_CACHE.get(key) != mtime:
            _ABORT_CACHE[key] = mtime
            log(f"[!] abort file detected: {ctx.args.abort_file} "
                f"(mtime {mtime})", err=True)
        if mtime:
            return True
    return ctx.instability is not None and ctx.instability.aborted

Add before def fetch(self, ...):

python
    def _throttle(self) -> None:
        if self.min_interval <= 0:
            return
        with self._rl_lock:
            wait = self._rl_last + self.min_interval - time.monotonic()
            if wait > 0:
                time.sleep(wait)
            self._rl_last = time.monotonic()

    def _abort_check(self) -> bool:
        f = getattr(self, "_abort_fn", None)
        return bool(f and f())

Simpler solution: wrap the entire fetch body:

python
def fetch(self, ...):
    if self._abort_check():
        raise SystemExit(3)
    self._throttle()
    resp = self._fetch_inner(...)
    if resp is not None and self.instability is not None:
        self.instability.observe(resp.status)
    return resp

def _fetch_inner(self, ...):
    # the existing body

@dataclass
class Ctx:
    http: HttpClient
    args: argparse.Namespace
    base_url: str
    collab: Optional[Collab] = None
    tech: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    pages: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    discovered: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    endpoints: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    tokens: List[Tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    root: str = ""
    extra_seeds: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    extra_discovered: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    source_maps: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    hidden_params: List[Tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    external_hosts: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    activity: Optional[ActivityLog] = None
    instability: Optional[InstabilityMonitor] = None
    login_form: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    login_page_url: str = ""
    authed_client: Optional[HttpClient] = None
5. Login / session helpers — add after build_points
python
def find_login_form(ctx: Ctx):
    if ctx.login_form is not None:
        return ctx.login_page_url, ctx.login_form
    for page in ctx.pages:
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            fields = f["inputs"]
            if any(LOGIN_USER_RE.search(k) for k in fields) and \
                    any(LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k) for k in fields):
                ctx.login_page_url = page["url"]
                ctx.login_form = f
                return page["url"], f
    return None, None


def _fill_login(f: Dict[str, Any], email: str, password: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    params = {}
    for k, v in f["inputs"].items():
        if LOGIN_USER_RE.search(k) and not LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k):
            params[k] = email
        elif LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k):
            params[k] = password
        else:
            params[k] = v
    return params


def _refresh_csrf(client: HttpClient, page_url: str, f: Dict[str, Any],
                  params: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, str]:
    if not any(CSRF_FIELD_RE.search(k) for k in params):
        return params
    page = client.fetch(page_url, follow=True)
    if not page:
        return params
    _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
    want = urllib.parse.urlsplit(f["action"]).path
    for g in forms:
        if urllib.parse.urlsplit(g["action"]).path != want:
            continue
        for k, v in g["inputs"].items():
            if CSRF_FIELD_RE.search(k):
                params[k] = v
        break
    return params


def auto_login_into(client: HttpClient, ctx: Ctx, email: str, password: str):
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return False, "no login form"
    params = _fill_login(f, email, password)
    params = _refresh_csrf(client, page_url, f, params)
    r = client.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return False, "request failed"
    if r.status >= 400:
        return False, f"HTTP {r.status}"
    if re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|denied)", r.text[:3000]):
        return False, "rejected"
    return True, r.url


def get_authed_client(ctx: Ctx) -> Optional[HttpClient]:
    if ctx.authed_client is not None:
        return ctx.authed_client
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return None
    c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(c, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return None
    ctx.authed_client = c
    return c


def _preflight(ctx: Ctx) -> Optional[Finding]:
    """Return a blocking finding if operational gates are not satisfied."""
    if not in_testing_window(ctx.args.testing_hours):
        return Finding("gate", "info", "Outside testing window",
                       ctx.base_url,
                       evidence=f"window={ctx.args.testing_hours}, current="
                                f"{time.strftime('%H:%M')}",
                       remediation="Rerun inside the approved window.",
                       confidence="high", phase=2)
    if ctx.instability is not None and ctx.instability.aborted:
        return Finding("gate", "info", "Aborted: instability threshold exceeded",
                       ctx.base_url,
                       evidence=f"{ctx.instability.errors}/{ctx.instability.total} 5xx "
                                f"responses (threshold {ctx.instability.threshold:.0%})",
                       confidence="high", phase=2)
    return None
6. Test cases A through G — add a new section
python
# =========================================================================== #
# PHASE 2 - authentication and session management
# =========================================================================== #

def check_password_policy(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """A1 - weak password acceptance at registration. Opt-in only."""
    if not ctx.args.password_policy_test:
        return []
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return [Finding("authn", "info", "A1 password policy not tested",
                        ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="--password-policy-test set without --test-email",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]
    reg = None
    for page in ctx.pages:
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            if not any(LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k) for k in f["inputs"]):
                continue
            if not any(LOGIN_USER_RE.search(k) for k in f["inputs"]):
                continue
            if re.search(r"(?i)register|signup|sign-up|create", page["url"]) or \
                    re.search(r"(?i)register|signup|sign-up", f["action"]):
                reg = (page["url"], f)
                break
        if reg:
            break
    if not reg:
        return [Finding("authn", "info", "A1 no registration form found", ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="searched crawled pages for register/signup forms",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]
    page_url, f = reg
    for pw in WEAK_PASSWORDS[:3]:
        params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, pw)
        params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                           follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        rejected = re.search(r"(?i)(weak|too short|minimum|policy|invalid|reject|error)",
                             r.text[:3000]) or r.status >= 400
        if not rejected:
            return [Finding("authn", "medium", "Weak password accepted at registration",
                            f["action"], method="POST", payload=pw,
                            evidence=f"registration of {ctx.args.test_email} accepted "
                                     f"password of length {len(pw)}: {pw!r}",
                            remediation="Enforce 12+ chars, block breached passwords "
                                        "(HIBP k-anonymity API), reject common strings.",
                            phase=2)]
    return []


def check_enumeration(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """A2 + B4 - login and reset responses for known vs unknown accounts."""
    out = []
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return [Finding("authn", "info", "A2/B4 enumeration not tested", ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="--test-email not provided", confidence="high",
                        phase=2)]
    unknown = f"wp-{rand_token('', 10)}@wp-unused.example"
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return out

    def attempt(email: str):
        params = _fill_login(f, email, "wrongpw" + rand_token("", 8))
        params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                           follow=False)
        return r, time.monotonic() - t0

    known, t_known = attempt(ctx.args.test_email)
    unknown_r, t_unknown = attempt(unknown)
    if known and unknown_r:
        status_diff = known.status != unknown_r.status
        body_diff = similar(known.text, unknown_r.text) < 0.9
        size_diff = abs(len(known.body) - len(unknown_r.body)) > 50
        time_diff = abs(t_known - t_unknown) > 0.4
        if status_diff or body_diff or size_diff or time_diff:
            out.append(Finding(
                "enum", "medium", "Username/email enumeration via login",
                f["action"], method="POST",
                evidence=f"known: HTTP {known.status}, {len(known.body)}B, "
                         f"{t_known*1000:.0f}ms; unknown: HTTP {unknown_r.status}, "
                         f"{len(unknown_r.body)}B, {t_unknown*1000:.0f}ms",
                remediation="Return identical responses, sizes, and timing for known "
                            "and unknown accounts; do password verification last.",
                phase=2))

    reset = _find_reset_form(ctx)
    if reset:
        page_url, f2 = reset

        def reset_attempt(email: str):
            params = _fill_login(f2, email, "")
            params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f2, params)
            r = ctx.http.fetch(f2["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                               follow=False)
            return r

        k = reset_attempt(ctx.args.test_email)
        u = reset_attempt(unknown)
        if k and u:
            if k.status != u.status or similar(k.text, u.text) < 0.9 or \
                    abs(len(k.body) - len(u.body)) > 50:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "enum", "medium", "Username/email enumeration via password reset",
                    f2["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence=f"known: HTTP {k.status}, {len(k.body)}B; "
                             f"unknown: HTTP {u.status}, {len(u.body)}B",
                    remediation="Always return the same message for password reset "
                                "requests.", phase=2))
    return out


def check_bruteforce(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """A3 - bounded rate-limit / lockout probe on login."""
    if not ctx.args.rate_test:
        return []
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    n = min(ctx.args.rate_count, 25)
    statuses, headers_429, elapsed = [], 0, 0.0
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    for _ in range(n):
        params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, "wrongpw" + rand_token("", 8))
        params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                           follow=False)
        if r is None:
            break
        statuses.append(r.status)
        if r.status == 429 or r.header("Retry-After"):
            headers_429 += 1
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
    limited = headers_429 > 0 or any(s in (429, 403, 503) for s in statuses)
    if not limited and len(statuses) >= n:
        return [Finding("bruteforce", "medium", "No login rate limiting observed",
                        f["action"], method="POST",
                        evidence=f"{len(statuses)} failed attempts in {elapsed:.1f}s "
                                 f"without 429/403/Retry-After; "
                                 f"statuses={sorted(set(statuses))}",
                        remediation="Add per-account and per-IP throttling with "
                                    "exponential backoff and alerting.", phase=2)]
    return []


def check_default_creds(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """A5 - bounded default credential check on the admin login."""
    if not ctx.args.admin_login:
        return []
    out = []
    for user, pw in DEFAULT_CREDS:
        data = {"username": user, "password": pw, "email": user, "login": user,
                "user": user, "pass": pw}
        r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.args.admin_login, "POST",
                           urllib.parse.urlencode(data), follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status >= 500:
            continue
        if r.status < 400 and not re.search(
                r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|error|denied|forbidden)",
                r.text[:3000]):
            out.append(Finding(
                "default-creds", "critical", "Default admin credentials accepted",
                ctx.args.admin_login, method="POST", payload=f"{user}:{pw}",
                evidence=f"HTTP {r.status} with no rejection markers; "
                         f"final URL: {r.url}",
                remediation="Remove default accounts, enforce MFA on admin login, "
                            "and audit for similar accounts.",
                confidence="medium", phase=2))
            break
    return out


def _find_reset_form(ctx: Ctx):
    for page in ctx.pages:
        if not RESET_URL_RE.search(page["url"]):
            continue
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if f["method"] == "POST" and \
                    any(LOGIN_USER_RE.search(k) for k in f["inputs"]):
                return page["url"], f
    return None


def check_reset_token(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """B1 - reset token freshness / entropy (partial; email delivery not observed)."""
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return []
    reset = _find_reset_form(ctx)
    if not reset:
        return []
    page_url, f = reset
    tokens: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(2):
        params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, "")
        params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                           follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        m = RESET_TOKEN_RE.search(r.url) or RESET_TOKEN_RE.search(r.text)
        if m:
            tokens.append(m.group(1))
    if not tokens:
        return [Finding("reset", "info",
                        "B1 token not observable in reset response",
                        f["action"], method="POST",
                        evidence="token appears to be delivered by email; manual "
                                 "inspection of the message is required",
                        remediation="Manually retrieve the token from the test inbox "
                                    "and check entropy, single-use, and expiry.",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]
    out = []
    if len(tokens) >= 2 and tokens[0] == tokens[1]:
        out.append(Finding("reset", "high", "Reset token reused across requests",
                           f["action"], method="POST",
                           evidence=f"identical token on consecutive resets: "
                                    f"{tokens[0][:10]}...",
                           remediation="Generate a fresh CSPRNG token per request; "
                                       "invalidate on use and after expiry.",
                           phase=2))
    t = tokens[0]
    if len(t) < 16 or shannon(t) < 3.5:
        out.append(Finding("reset", "medium", "Low-entropy password reset token",
                           f["action"], method="POST",
                           evidence=f"length={len(t)}, shannon={shannon(t):.2f} bits/char",
                           remediation="Use ≥128 bits of entropy, base64url-encoded.",
                           phase=2))
    return out


def check_host_header_reset(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """B2 - Host / X-Forwarded-Host injection into reset flow."""
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return []
    reset = _find_reset_form(ctx)
    if not reset:
        return []
    page_url, f = reset
    out = []
    evil = f"wp-evil-{rand_token('', 6)}.example"
    for header in ("Host", "X-Forwarded-Host"):
        params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, "")
        params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
        r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                           headers={header: evil}, follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if evil in r.text or evil in r.url:
            out.append(Finding(
                "reset-host", "high",
                f"Host header injection in password reset ({header})",
                f["action"], method="POST", payload=f"{header}: {evil}",
                evidence=f"attacker-controlled host {evil} reflected in reset flow",
                remediation="Hard-code the canonical base URL for reset links; "
                            "ignore Host/X-Forwarded-Host from client input.",
                phase=2))
    return out


def check_session_fixation(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """C2 - session identifier rotation on login."""
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    fresh = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    fresh.fetch(page_url, follow=True)
    pre = {c.name: c.value for c in fresh.jar if SESSION_COOKIE_RE.search(c.name)}
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(fresh, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return []
    post = {c.name: c.value for c in fresh.jar if SESSION_COOKIE_RE.search(c.name)}
    out = []
    for name in pre:
        if name in post and pre[name] == post[name]:
            out.append(Finding(
                "session-fix", "high", "Session fixation: ID not rotated on login",
                f["action"], method="POST", param=name,
                evidence=f"cookie '{name}' unchanged across authentication",
                remediation="Issue a fresh session ID on every authentication state "
                            "change; invalidate the pre-auth ID server-side.",
                phase=2))
    return out


def check_logout_invalidation(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """C4 - server-side invalidation of the session on logout."""
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(c, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return []
    home = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    logout_url = None
    for link in parse_page(home.text, home.url)[0]:
        if re.search(r"(?i)logout|sign-out|signout", link):
            logout_url = link
            break
    if not logout_url:
        for p in ("/logout", "/signout", "/api/logout", "/api/auth/logout"):
            r = c.fetch(ctx.root + p, follow=True)
            if r and r.status < 400 and not re.search(r"(?i)404|not found", r.text[:2000]):
                logout_url = ctx.root + p
                break
    if not logout_url:
        return []
    pre = {ck.name: ck.value for ck in c.jar if SESSION_COOKIE_RE.search(ck.name)}
    c.fetch(logout_url, follow=True)
    replay_cookie = "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in pre.items())
    replay = ctx.http.clone(cookie=replay_cookie)
    r = replay.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is None or anon is None or r.status >= 400:
        return []
    if similar(anon.text, r.text) > 0.9:
        return []
    return [Finding("logout", "high", "Session not invalidated on logout",
                    logout_url,
                    evidence=f"replay of pre-logout cookie returned a distinct "
                             f"authenticated-looking response (HTTP {r.status})",
                    remediation="Invalidate server-side session state on logout; "
                                "clear cookies with matching Path/Domain.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=2)]


def check_concurrent_sessions(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """C5 - concurrent session policy."""
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return []
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []

    def login():
        c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
        ok, _ = auto_login_into(c, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
        return c, ok

    c1, ok1 = login()
    time.sleep(0.5)
    c2, ok2 = login()
    time.sleep(0.5)
    if not (ok1 and ok2):
        return []
    time.sleep(0.3)
    r1 = c1.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    r2 = c2.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon_text = anon.text if anon else ""
    v1 = r1 is not None and r1.status < 400 and similar(anon_text, r1.text) < 0.9
    v2 = r2 is not None and r2.status < 400 and similar(anon_text, r2.text) < 0.9
    return [Finding("session-conc", "info", "Concurrent sessions allowed",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence=f"two logins both valid after 1s: first={v1}, second={v2}",
                    remediation="Confirm this is intended policy; consider notifying "
                                "the user of new sign-ins.",
                    phase=2)]


def check_remember_me(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """C6 - persistent 'remember me' token characteristics."""
    out = []
    r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    for raw in r.header_all("Set-Cookie"):
        if not re.search(r"(?i)remember|persistent|stay-signed", raw) and \
           "Max-Age=0" not in raw and "Expires=" not in raw:
            continue
        name = raw.split("=", 1)[0].strip()
        val = raw.split("=", 1)[1].split(";", 1)[0] if "=" in raw else ""
        if len(val) < 8:
            continue
        if len(val) < 16 or shannon(val) < 3.0:
            out.append(Finding(
                "remember", "medium", f"Weak or low-entropy persistent cookie: {name}",
                r.url, param=name,
                evidence=f"value length={len(val)}, shannon={shannon(val):.2f}",
                remediation="Use ≥128-bit CSPRNG token; rotate on use; add "
                            "HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite.",
                phase=2))
    return out


def check_token_in_url(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """C7 - session token in URL (heuristic over discovered URLs)."""
    out = []
    pattern = re.compile(
        r"(?i)[?&](?:session|sid|sess|jwt|token|auth|access_token)=([A-Za-z0-9_\-.]{20,})")
    for url in ctx.discovered:
        m = pattern.search(url)
        if m:
            out.append(Finding("token-in-url", "medium", "Session token in URL", url,
                               param=m.group(0).split("=")[0],
                               evidence=f"token in query string, length {len(m.group(1))}",
                               remediation="Never place session tokens in URLs; use "
                                           "HttpOnly cookies or an Authorization header.",
                               phase=2))
    return out


def check_cache_controls(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """C8 - cache-control on authenticated responses."""
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    r = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return []
    cc = r.header("Cache-Control").lower()
    pragma = r.header("Pragma").lower()
    if "no-store" in cc or "no-cache" in cc or "private" in cc or "no-cache" in pragma:
        return []
    return [Finding("cache-ctrl", "low",
                    "Authenticated page lacks no-store / private cache directive",
                    r.url,
                    evidence=f"Cache-Control: {cc or '(unset)'}; "
                             f"Pragma: {pragma or '(unset)'}",
                    remediation="Send Cache-Control: no-store on authenticated "
                                "responses.", phase=2)]


def check_jwt_expiry(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """D4 - JWT exp claim present and reasonable."""
    out = []
    now = int(time.time())
    for name, tok in ctx.tokens[:4]:
        dec = decode_jwt(tok)
        if not dec:
            continue
        _, payload, _, _ = dec
        if "exp" not in payload:
            out.append(Finding("jwt", "medium", "JWT has no exp claim",
                               ctx.base_url, param=name,
                               evidence=f"claims: {list(payload)}",
                               remediation="Include exp and enforce it server-side.",
                               phase=2))
            continue
        exp = payload["exp"]
        if isinstance(exp, (int, float)) and exp - now > 30 * 86400:
            out.append(Finding("jwt", "low", "JWT expiry is unusually long",
                               ctx.base_url, param=name,
                               evidence=f"exp is {(exp - now) / 86400:.0f} days from now",
                               remediation="Use short-lived access tokens (≤1h) with "
                                           "refresh tokens.", phase=2))
    return out


def check_jwt_pii(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """D5 - sensitive/PII claims inside JWT payload."""
    out = []
    for name, tok in ctx.tokens[:4]:
        dec = decode_jwt(tok)
        if not dec:
            continue
        _, payload, _, _ = dec
        hits = [k for k in payload if any(p in k.lower() for p in PII_CLAIMS)]
        if hits:
            out.append(Finding("jwt", "medium", "Sensitive data in JWT payload",
                               ctx.base_url, param=name,
                               evidence=f"claims matching PII keywords: "
                                        f"{', '.join(hits)}",
                               remediation="JWTs are base64, not encrypted. Move PII "
                                           "out of the token payload.", phase=2))
    return out


def check_authz_customer(ctx: Ctx) -> List[Finding]:
    """G1/G2 - customer identity attempting admin routes."""
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    out = []
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    for path in ADMIN_PATHS_P2:
        url = ctx.root + path
        anon_r = anon.fetch(url, follow=True)
        r = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status >= 400:
            continue
        if re.search(r"(?i)(login|sign in|unauthorized|forbidden)", r.text[:2000]):
            continue
        if not ADMIN_MARKERS.search(r.text):
            continue
        anon_also = anon_r is not None and anon_r.status < 400 and \
                    ADMIN_MARKERS.search(anon_r.text)
        sev = "medium" if anon_also else "critical"
        out.append(Finding(
            "authz", sev,
            f"Customer role reaches admin surface: {path}" +
            (" (also reachable anonymously)" if anon_also else ""),
            url,
            evidence=f"HTTP {r.status} with admin markers "
                     f"({clip(r.text[:160], 160)})",
            remediation="Enforce role checks on every admin route and API "
                        "handler, not on the UI.", phase=2))
    return out

Manual checklist (do not skip)
These are the cases the tool flags as manual and the ones to execute by hand against your test accounts before Phase 3:

A4 credential stuffing — use a small synthetic list against provisioned test accounts only; watch for account lockout signals.

B3 reset reuse/expiry — retrieve the token from the test inbox, use it, replay it, wait past expiry, replay again.

B5 reset link leakage — inspect Referer from the reset page, mail headers, and the URL in any intermediate redirects.

C3 idle/absolute timeout — log in, do nothing for the approved idle threshold, then act; repeat to test absolute cap.

E1–E4 MFA/OTP — if MFA is present on the accounts you have, test bounded OTP guesses, OTP reuse, and direct-navigation bypass of the MFA prompt.

The activity log file (--activity-log) matches the format from your playbook — timestamp \t test_id \t outcome \t description \t evidence — so it can be appended to your deliverables matrix unchanged. The Finding records already carry phase=2 and use the same remediation and evidence fields the rest of the report uses.

Let me structure:

Verdict (one line)

Two options (close now, or move on)

Let me be careful about the F1/F2/F3 issue — this is real. check_csrf in v2 looks at all POST forms and flags those without tokens. Login forms typically don't have tokens (they're protected by SameSite cookies, not tokens), so the tool would flag login forms as "CSRF vulnerability" — that's a false positive in the auth context. And logout CSRF isn't tested at all. Password change CSRF isn't tested.

Also, check_csrf in v2 has a --csrf-submit mode that will actually POST to forms. If run against login forms with fake credentials, that's a bunch of failed logins which could trigger lockout. Real gaps I'd close
1. F1/F2/F3 are wrong or missing.
The v2 check_csrf flags every POST form without a token. That's correct for state-changing forms, but login forms typically don't have CSRF tokens — they're protected by SameSite cookies instead. So the tool would report login forms as "POST form without anti-CSRF token," which is a false positive in the auth context. Worse, --csrf-submit will actually POST to the login form with fake credentials, which could trip lockout.

What's actually needed:

F1 login CSRF — test the right mechanism: send a login POST from a forged Origin/Referer and check whether the server accepts it. If SameSite=Lax/Strict is set and enforced, it's mitigated regardless of tokens.

F2 logout CSRF — GET /logout reachable without a token from a forged origin is the finding.

F3 password/email change CSRF — find the change-password / change-email forms (in the authed client) and check token presence + Origin enforcement. These are the highest-impact CSRF targets and are completely uncovered right now.

2. MFA/OTP is 0%.
Your playbook lists E1–E4 as in-scope "if present." The tool doesn't even detect whether MFA exists. At minimum: after a successful login with test creds, check whether the post-login response is a challenge page (input named otp/code/totp/mfa), a redirect to /mfa or /verify, or a session cookie issued without the MFA step. If MFA exists, E1 (bounded OTP guessing, rate-limited) and E3 (skip-MFA-by-direct-navigation) are automatable and bounded. E2 and E4 need manual mailbox/inbox access.

3. Supabase-specific checks.
You told me Supabase is in the stack. Nothing in Phase 2 touches it. Supabase auth tokens are JWTs with known claims (sub, email, role, aud, exp, session_id). Missing:

Access token appearing in URL fragment (very common in Supabase redirects)

Refresh token in localStorage / persistent cookie without rotation

RLS enforcement probed by calling /rest/v1/<table> with the test account's token and looking for rows that shouldn't be visible (this is G3-adjacent but the current check_idor doesn't touch it)

Default-deny check: unauthenticated call to /rest/v1/<table> should 401, not return data

4. Password change without current password, email change flow.
Both are account-takeover primitives and both are standard Phase 2 items. Neither is covered. check_authz_customer is about access, not auth integrity.

5. Coverage of "remember me" binding and revocation.
check_remember_me only checks entropy and flags. It doesn't test: does the persistent token survive a password change? Is it bound to a device/IP? Is it revocable server-side? The first is automatable (change password with the test account, then try the old remember-me cookie). The rest are manual.

If the user follows my instructions literally, ALL_CHECKS will not include the Phase 2 checks, and --profile full will silently skip them. HttpClient.fetch refactor — I described splitting into fetch() + _fetch_inner() for the instability monitor, but never provided the refactored code. Without it, the instability monitor never observes anything, and the abort-by-5xx-rate threshold never fires. This is the safety gate from your playbook; it must work.

sys.exit(3) on abort — the fetch path raises SystemExit(3) when the abort file is present, but main() doesn't catch it. The process dies with a traceback instead of the clean exit the activity log expects.

For the HttpClient refactor, I need to preserve existing behavior. The current fetch has a loop with redirect following. I'll wrap the whole thing.

python
def fetch(self, url, method="GET", data=None, headers=None, follow=True, timeout=None):
    if self._abort_check():
        raise SystemExit(3)
    self._throttle()
    resp = self._fetch_inner(url, method, data, headers, follow, timeout)
    if resp is not None and self.instability is not None:
        self.instability.observe(resp.status)
    return resp

def _fetch_inner(self, url, method="GET", data=None, headers=None, follow=True, timeout=None):
    # existing fetch body

For check_login_csrf — let me think about what a real login CSRF test looks like:

python
def check_login_csrf(ctx):
    # 1. Find login form
    # 2. Check if login POST succeeds with forged Origin (attacker's origin)
    # 3. If it does AND session cookies lack SameSite=Strict/Lax → CSRF possible
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return []  # can't test without valid creds
    # check current cookies for SameSite
    r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    cookie_headers = r.header_all("Set-Cookie") if r else []
    has_samesite = any(re.search(r"(?i)samesite\s*=\s*(lax|strict)", c) for c in cookie_headers)
    
    # Try login with forged Origin
    params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
    forged_headers = {"Origin": "https://wp-attacker.example", "Referer": "https://wp-attacker.example/"}
    fresh = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    r = fresh.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), headers=forged_headers, follow=True)
    if r is None or r.status >= 400:
        return []
    # If login succeeded despite forged origin, and SameSite not set → CSRF
    if re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|denied)", r.text[:3000]):
        return []  # rejected despite forged origin — but that could be creds issue
    if not has_samesite:
        return [Finding(
            "login-csrf", "low",
            "Login form accepts POST from a forged Origin without SameSite cookies",
            f["action"], method="POST",
            evidence=f"login POST from Origin: https://wp-attacker.example was accepted; "
                     f"session cookies lack SameSite=Lax/Strict",
            remediation="Set SameSite=Lax/Strict on session cookies; validate Origin/Referer "
                        "on state-changing requests.",
            confidence="medium",
            phase=2)]
    return []
That's reasonable. Might have false positives if login has other protections, but confidence is set to medium.

def check_logout_csrf(ctx):
    # Find a logout link (GET or POST)
    # Try requesting it with forged Origin without CSRF token
    # If logout succeeds from forged origin → CSRF
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    home = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    logout_url = None
    logout_method = "GET"
    for link in parse_page(home.text, home.url)[0]:
        if re.search(r"(?i)logout|sign-out|signout", link):
            logout_url = link
            break
    if not logout_url:
        return []
    # Try with forged origin, no auth cookie (we're testing whether the endpoint 
    # requires auth or CSRF tokens)
    # Actually — the CSRF risk is: victim is logged in, attacker's page makes 
    # request to logout URL. Browser sends cookies. So test: does logout work 
    # when Origin is forged but cookie is present?
    forged = {"Origin": "https://wp-attacker.example", "Referer": "https://wp-attacker.example/"}
    before = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    r = c.fetch(logout_url, "GET", headers=forged, follow=True)
    after = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    # If we're now logged out (after looks like anonymous)
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if after and anon and similar(anon.text, after.text) > 0.9:
        return [Finding(
            "logout-csrf", "low",
            "Logout via GET works from a forged Origin without CSRF token",
            logout_url,
            evidence="logout succeeded with Origin/Referer set to an attacker domain; "
                     "session invalidated",
            remediation="Require a POST with a CSRF token for logout, or at minimum "
                        "validate Origin/Referer.",
            phase=2)]
    return []

def check_logout_csrf(ctx):
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    # Clone credentials into a fresh client
    tester = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(tester, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return []
    home = tester.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    logout_url = None
    for link in parse_page(home.text, home.url)[0]:
        if re.search(r"(?i)logout|sign-out|signout", link):
            logout_url = link
            break
    if not logout_url:
        return []
    forged = {"Origin": "https://wp-attacker.example", "Referer": "https://wp-attacker.example/"}
    r = tester.fetch(logout_url, "GET", headers=forged, follow=True)
    after = tester.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
