For check_auth_change_csrf — finds password/email change forms in authed pages.

python
def check_auth_change_csrf(ctx):
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    out = []
    # Look for forms in authenticated pages
    home = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    # Find change-password / change-email pages
    candidates = []
    for link in parse_page(home.text, home.url)[0]:
        if re.search(r"(?i)(password|email|account|profile|settings)", link):
            candidates.append(link)
    candidates.append(ctx.root + "/account/password")
    candidates.append(ctx.root + "/account/email")
    candidates.append(ctx.root + "/settings/password")
    candidates.append(ctx.root + "/profile/settings")
    
    seen_actions = set()
    for url in dict.fromkeys(candidates):
        page = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if page is None or page.status >= 400:
            continue
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        for f in forms:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            if urllib.parse.urlsplit(f["action"]).path in seen_actions:
                continue
            seen_actions.add(urllib.parse.urlsplit(f["action"]).path)
            fields = f["inputs"]
            is_pw = any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?pass|confirm.?pass)", k) for k in fields) and \
                    any(re.search(r"(?i)pass", k) for k in fields)
            is_email = any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?email|email)", k) for k in fields) and \
                       any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|password)", k) for k in fields)
            if not (is_pw or is_email):
                continue
            tok = [k for k in fields if CSRF_FIELD_RE.search(k)]
            kind = "password change" if is_pw else "email change"
            if not tok:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "auth-change-csrf", "high",
                    f"{kind} form without anti-CSRF token",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence=f"fields: {', '.join(list(fields)[:8])}",
                    remediation="Require a per-session, unpredictable CSRF token validated "
                                "server-side; set SameSite=Lax on session cookies.",
                    phase=2))
            # Check current-password requirement
            if is_pw and not any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|existing)", k) for k in fields):
                out.append(Finding(
                    "auth-change-csrf", "high",
                    "Password change does not require current password",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence="no current/old password field present",
                    remediation="Require the current password before setting a new one.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=2))
            if is_email and not any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|password)", k) for k in fields):
                out.append(Finding(
                    "auth-change-csrf", "high",
                    "Email change does not require current password",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence="no current password or confirmation step detected",
                    remediation="Require the current password and confirm via the old address.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=2))
    return out
Good.

For MFA detection, add helper:

python
MFA_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(/mfa|/2fa|/otp|/verify|/totp|/challenge|/step-up|/second-factor)")
MFA_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)^(otp|code|totp|mfa|2fa|auth.?code|verification.?code|"
                         r"token|digit)$")

def _login_and_classify(ctx):
    """Return (client, outcome) where outcome is one of:
    'no_form', 'no_creds', 'failed', 'rejected', 'authed', 'mfa'."""
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return None, "no_form"
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return None, "no_creds"
    c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    params = _refresh_csrf(c, page_url, f, params)
    r = c.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return None, "failed"
    if MFA_URL_RE.search(r.url) or MFA_URL_RE.search(r.header("Location")):
        return c, "mfa"
    # Look for an MFA prompt in the body
    try:
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(r.text, r.url)
    except Exception:
        forms = []
    for form in forms:
        if any(MFA_FIELD_RE.match(k) for k in form["inputs"]):
            return c, "mfa"
    if r.status >= 400:
        return c, "failed"
    if re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|denied)", r.text[:3000]):
        return c, "rejected"
    return c, "authed"
Then check_mfa_presence:

python
def check_mfa_presence(ctx):
    _, outcome = _login_and_classify(ctx)
    if outcome == "no_form":
        return []
    if outcome == "no_creds":
        return [Finding("mfa", "info",
                        "MFA presence not tested (no test credentials)",
                        ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="--test-email/--test-password not provided",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]
    if outcome == "mfa":
        return [Finding("mfa", "info", "MFA challenge detected after login",
                        ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="post-login flow redirected to an MFA/OTP endpoint "
                                 "or served an MFA/OTP form",
                        remediation="E1 (bounded OTP guessing) and E3 (MFA bypass) "
                                    "can be tested with --otp-test; E2/E4 need the "
                                    "test inbox.",
                        phase=2)]
    if outcome == "authed":
        return [Finding("mfa", "medium",
                        "No MFA challenge after successful password login",
                        ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="successful login issued a session without an MFA step",
                        remediation="Require MFA on all privileged accounts (admin, staff) "
                                    "and at least offer it to customers.",
                        phase=2)]
    return []
For check_mfa_bypass — needs MFA flow + pre-MFA client:

python
def check_mfa_bypass(ctx):
    if not ctx.args.test_email:
        return []
    c, outcome = _login_and_classify(ctx)
    if outcome != "mfa" or c is None:
        return []
    out = []
    # Try authenticated pages with the pre-MFA client
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon_text = anon.text if anon else ""
    for path in ["/account", "/dashboard", "/orders", "/bookings", "/profile"] + ADMIN_PATHS_P2[:6]:
        url = ctx.root + path
        r = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status >= 400:
            continue
        if MFA_URL_RE.search(r.url) or MFA_URL_RE.search(r.header("Location")):
            continue
        if similar(anon_text, r.text) > 0.9:
            continue
        if re.search(r"(?i)(login|sign in|unauthorized|forbidden)", r.text[:2000]):
            continue
        out.append(Finding(
            "mfa", "high", f"MFA bypass: {path} accessible before MFA verification",
            url,
            evidence=f"HTTP {r.status} with substantive body "
                     f"({clip(r.text[:160], 160)})",
            confidence="medium",
            phase=2))
        if len(out) >= 3:
            break
    return out
For check_otp_bruteforce — opt-in, bounded:

python
def check_otp_bruteforce(ctx):
    if not ctx.args.otp_test:
        return []
    c, outcome = _login_and_classify(ctx)
    if outcome != "mfa" or c is None:
        return []
    # Find the OTP form
    home = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    _, forms, _ = parse_page(home.text, home.url)
    otp_form = None
    for f in forms:
        if any(MFA_FIELD_RE.match(k) for k in f["inputs"]):
            otp_form = f
            break
    if not otp_form:
        return []
    n = min(ctx.args.rate_count, 12)
    codes = ["000000", "111111", "123456", "654321", "999999", "0000", "1111",
             "1234", "00000000", "12345678"]
    statuses, elapsed = [], 0.0
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    for i in range(n):
        params = {k: v for k, v in otp_form["inputs"].items()}
        for k in params:
            if MFA_FIELD_RE.match(k):
                params[k] = codes[i % len(codes)]
        r = c.fetch(otp_form["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), follow=True)
        if r is None:
            break
        statuses.append(r.status)
        if r.status == 429 or r.header("Retry-After"):
            break
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
    if len(statuses) >= n and not any(s in (429, 403, 503) for s in statuses):
        return [Finding(
            "mfa", "high", "No rate limit on OTP submissions",
            otp_form["action"], method="POST",
            evidence=f"{len(statuses)} OTP guesses in {elapsed:.1f}s without 429/Retry-After",
            remediation="Throttle OTP attempts per session/account; lock or lock out "
                        "after 3–5 failures; require MFA re-initiation.",
            phase=2)]
    return []
For check_supabase:

python
def check_supabase(ctx):
    out = []
    # 1. Fragment tokens in HTML
    for page in ctx.pages:
        if "#access_token=" in page.get("html", "") or \
           "#refresh_token=" in page.get("html", ""):
            out.append(Finding(
                "supabase", "high", "Supabase access/refresh token in URL fragment",
                page["url"],
                evidence="response body contains #access_token= or #refresh_token=",
                remediation="Use the PKCE flow with a cookie-bound state; avoid "
                            "implicit-flow fragment tokens.",
                phase=2))
            break
    # 2. supabase.co references
    sb_hosts = set()
    for url in ctx.discovered + ctx.endpoints:
        m = re.search(r"https?://([a-z0-9\-]+)\.supabase\.co", url)
        if m:
            sb_hosts.add(m.group(0))
    for h in list(sb_hosts)[:5]:
        # 3. rest/v1 unauth check
        probe = h.rstrip("/") + "/rest/v1/"
        r = ctx.http.fetch(probe, follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if r.status == 200 and re.search(r"(?i)(table|openapi|swagger|paths)", r.text):
            out.append(Finding(
                "supabase", "high", "Supabase /rest/v1/ reachable unauthenticated",
                probe,
                evidence=f"HTTP 200 with schema/tables disclosed",
                remediation="Enable Row-Level Security on every table and require "
                            "auth.uid() in policies. Anonymous SELECT should be denied "
                            "by default.",
                phase=2))
        # 4. RLS probe with test token (if we have one)
        if ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password:
            # Supabase auth: POST /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password
            sb_ref = re.search(r"https://([a-z0-9\-]+)\.supabase\.co", h)
            if sb_ref:
                anon_key = _find_supabase_anon_key(ctx.pages)
                if anon_key:
                    tok = _supabase_login(h, anon_key, ctx.args.test_email,
                                         ctx.args.test_password)
                    if tok:
                        out += _supabase_rls_probe(ctx, h, anon_key, tok)
    return out


def _find_supabase_anon_key(pages):
    for page in pages:
        html = page.get("html", "")
        # anon keys are JWTs with role=anon
        for m in re.finditer(r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}", html):
            dec = decode_jwt(m.group(0))
            if dec and dec[1].get("role") == "anon":
                return m.group(0)
    return None


def _supabase_login(sb_host, anon_key, email, password):
    r = HttpClient().fetch(
        sb_host.rstrip("/") + "/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password",
        "POST",
        json.dumps({"email": email, "password": password}),
        headers={"apikey": anon_key, "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    if r is None or r.status != 200:
        return None
    try:
        data = json.loads(r.text)
        return data.get("access_token")
    except Exception:
        return None


def _supabase_rls_probe(ctx, sb_host, anon_key, access_token):
    out = []
    # Try to enumerate tables from /rest/v1/ openapi
    r = ctx.http.fetch(sb_host.rstrip("/") + "/rest/v1/",
                       headers={"apikey": anon_key,
                                "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
                       follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    tables = re.findall(r"/rest/v1/([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", r.text)
    for tbl in list(dict.fromkeys(tables))[:8]:
        url = sb_host.rstrip("/") + f"/rest/v1/{tbl}?select=*&limit=5"
        rr = ctx.http.fetch(url,
                            headers={"apikey": anon_key,
                                     "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
                            follow=True)
        if rr is None or rr.status != 200:
            continue
        try:
            rows = json.loads(rr.text)
        except Exception:
            continue
        if isinstance(rows, list) and len(rows) > 0:
            # Check if any row has a user_id/sub that isn't ours
            our_sub = None
            dec = decode_jwt(access_token)
            if dec:
                our_sub = dec[1].get("sub")
            foreign = [row for row in rows
                       if isinstance(row, dict) and
                       row.get("user_id") and row.get("user_id") != our_sub]
            if foreign:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "supabase", "critical",
                    f"RLS bypass: rows readable outside test account in '{tbl}'",
                    url,
                    evidence=f"{len(rows)} rows returned; "
                             f"{len(foreign)} with foreign user_id",
                    remediation="Every table must have RLS enabled with policies "
                                "scoped to auth.uid(); verify with SET ROLE.",
                    confidence="high", phase=2))
    return out
That's a lot. Let me trim — the RLS probe is nice but complex, maybe keep it but simpler.

Actually let me keep it but make it clearer.

For check_password_change:

python
def check_password_change(ctx):
    """Detect change-password flows; destructive checks opt-in via --destructive."""
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    out = []
    # Find change password form
    targets = [ctx.root + p for p in
               ("/account/password", "/settings/password", "/profile/password",
                "/account/security", "/settings/security")]
    found_form = None
    for url in targets:
        page = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if page is None or page.status >= 400:
            continue
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        for f in forms:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            fields = f["inputs"]
            if any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?pass|confirm.?pass|password1|newpassword)", k)
                   for k in fields):
                found_form = f
                break
        if found_form:
            break
    if not found_form:
        return []
    fields = found_form["inputs"]
    if not any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|existing)", k) for k in fields):
        out.append(Finding(
            "password-change", "high",
            "Password change form does not require current password",
            found_form["action"], method="POST",
            evidence=f"fields: {', '.join(list(fields)[:8])}",
            remediation="Require the current password before accepting a new one.",
            phase=2))
    if not ctx.args.destructive:
        return out
    # Destructive: actually change the password, then verify old remember-me dies
    old_pass = ctx.args.test_password
    new_pass = old_pass + "X" + rand_token("", 4)
    params = {}
    for k, v in fields.items():
        if re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|existing)", k):
            params[k] = old_pass
        elif re.search(r"(?i)(new.?pass|password1|newpassword)", k):
            params[k] = new_pass
        elif re.search(r"(?i)confirm", k):
            params[k] = new_pass
        else:
            params[k] = v
    params = _refresh_csrf(c, url, found_form, params)
    r = c.fetch(found_form["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    if re.search(r"(?i)(success|updated|changed)", r.text[:2000]):
        out.append(Finding(
            "password-change", "info", "Password change submitted (destructive test)",
            found_form["action"], method="POST",
            evidence="password changed; original credential preserved in "
                     "ctx.args.test_password, new credential in activity log",
            remediation="Restore the test account password after the run.",
            phase=2))
    return out
Hmm, destructive flag with password change is dangerous. Let me make it very clear in the flag help. Actually the flag --destructive might be too broad. Let me use --test-password-change specifically.

Also — this modifies the test account which could break subsequent checks. Best to note this in the flag help.

For check_email_change:

python
def check_email_change(ctx):
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    out = []
    targets = [ctx.root + p for p in
               ("/account/email", "/settings/email", "/profile/email",
                "/account/settings", "/settings/account")]
    for url in targets:
        page = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if page is None or page.status >= 400:
            continue
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        for f in forms:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            fields = f["inputs"]
            if not any(re.search(r"(?i)email", k) for k in fields):
                continue
            # Must be a "new email" form (not search)
            if not any(re.search(r"(?i)(new|change|update)", k) for k in fields):
                continue
            needs_confirm = any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|password|verify|confirm)", k)
                                for k in fields)
            if not needs_confirm:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "email-change", "high",
                    "Email change form does not require current password",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence=f"fields: {', '.join(list(fields)[:8])}",
                    remediation="Require the current password and confirm via the "
                                "old address before switching.",
                    phase=2))
            break
    return out
Good.

    def fetch(self, url, method="GET", data=None, headers=None, follow=True,
              timeout=None) -> Optional[Response]:
        if self._abort_check():
            raise SystemExit(3)
        self._throttle()
        resp = self._fetch_inner(url, method, data, headers, follow, timeout)
        if resp is not None and self.instability is not None:
            self.instability.observe(resp.status)
        return resp

Let me be more careful about this check. The realistic outcome is:

If creds valid and Origin forged → login succeeds → CSRF vulnerability

If creds invalid → always rejected → can't test

If Origin is enforced → rejected with 403/CSRF error → mitigated

So this check requires valid test creds. Should be gated on them.

Also — a real login CSRF attack logs the victim into the attacker's account, which is different from "attacker can submit login form on behalf of victim." The check I wrote is more about "does the server enforce Origin for login POST." That's actually the right check for the mitigation. Let me keep it but frame it correctly.

Fix 1 — HttpClient.fetch refactor
The instability monitor never fires without this. Replace the existing fetch method with a wrapper plus _fetch_inner containing the unchanged original body:

python
    def fetch(self, url, method="GET", data=None, headers=None, follow=True,
              timeout=None) -> Optional[Response]:
        if self._abort_check():
            raise SystemExit(3)
        self._throttle()
        resp = self._fetch_inner(url, method, data, headers, follow, timeout)
        if resp is not None and self.instability is not None:
            self.instability.observe(resp.status)
        return resp

    def _fetch_inner(self, url, method="GET", data=None, headers=None, follow=True,
                     timeout=None) -> Optional[Response]:
        # ---- unchanged body of the original fetch() ----
        url = ensure_scheme(url)
        method = method.upper()
        ...
        return resp
The only line removed from the original is the trailing return resp — everything else stays identical.

Fix 2 — Registry ordering

GLOBAL_EARLY = {
    "headers": (6, check_headers),
    "cors": (6, check_cors),
    "files": (6, check_files),

Fix 3 — SystemExit handling and activity logging in main()
Replace the three run loops with:

python
    def _run_global_loop(table):
        out = []
        for name in list(table):
            if name not in checks:
                continue
            if args.abort_file and os.path.exists(args.abort_file):
                log("[!] abort file present; stopping", err=True)
                return out
            try:
                out += run_global(ctx, name, table)
                if ctx.activity:
                    ctx.activity.record(name, "run",
                                        PHASE_NAMES.get(table[name][0], ""))
            except SystemExit:
                log(f"[!] abort during {name}", err=True)
                return out
        return out

    findings += _run_global_loop(GLOBAL_EARLY)

    # ... crawl block unchanged ...

    findings += _run_global_loop(GLOBAL_LATE)

    # point-check loop:
    if any(c in POINT_CHECKS for c in checks):
        points = build_points(pages, ctx.discovered, args.max_points)
        ...
        try:
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, args.threads)) as ex:
                futures = {ex.submit(run_point_check, ctx, pt, n): (pt, n)
                           for pt, n in jobs}
                for fut in as_completed(futures):
                    findings += fut.result()
        except SystemExit:
            log("[!] abort during point checks", err=True)
New helper — _login_and_classify
Add after get_authed_client:

python
MFA_URL_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)(/mfa|/2fa|/otp|/verify|/totp|/challenge|/step-up|"
                       r"/second-factor|/auth/code)")
MFA_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"(?i)^(otp|code|totp|mfa|2fa|auth.?code|verification.?code|"
                         r"token|digit)$")


def _login_and_classify(ctx) -> Tuple[Optional[HttpClient], str]:
    """Return (client, outcome). outcome in:
    'no_form', 'no_creds', 'failed', 'rejected', 'authed', 'mfa'."""
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return None, "no_form"
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return None, "no_creds"
    c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    params = _refresh_csrf(c, page_url, f, params)
    r = c.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params), follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return None, "failed"
    if MFA_URL_RE.search(r.url) or MFA_URL_RE.search(r.header("Location")):
        return c, "mfa"
    try:
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(r.text, r.url)
    except Exception:
        forms = []
    for form in forms:
        if any(MFA_FIELD_RE.match(k) for k in form["inputs"]):
            return c, "mfa"
    if r.status >= 400:
        return c, "failed"
    if re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|denied)", r.text[:3000]):
        return c, "rejected"
    return c, "authed"
F1 — check_login_csrf
python
def check_login_csrf(ctx):
    """F1 - login CSRF / Origin enforcement on the login POST."""
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return [Finding("login-csrf", "info",
                        "F1 login CSRF not tested (no test credentials)",
                        ctx.base_url, evidence="--test-email/--test-password not set",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]

    # baseline: is there a SameSite cookie on the app at all?
    r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    cookie_headers = r.header_all("Set-Cookie") if r else []
    has_samesite = any(re.search(r"(?i)samesite\s*=\s*(lax|strict)", c)
                       for c in cookie_headers)

    params = _fill_login(f, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    params = _refresh_csrf(ctx.http, page_url, f, params)
    forged = {"Origin": "https://wp-csrf-attacker.example",
              "Referer": "https://wp-csrf-attacker.example/"}
    fresh = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    resp = fresh.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                       headers=forged, follow=True)
    if resp is None or resp.status >= 400:
        return []
    if re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|denied)", resp.text[:3000]):
        return []

    if not has_samesite:
        return [Finding(
            "login-csrf", "medium",
            "Login accepts forged-Origin POST without SameSite cookies",
            f["action"], method="POST",
            evidence="login with Origin/Referer forged to wp-csrf-attacker.example "
                     "succeeded; session cookies lack SameSite=Lax/Strict",
            remediation="Set SameSite=Lax/Strict on session cookies and validate "
                        "Origin/Referer on login POST.",
            phase=2)]
    return [Finding(
        "login-csrf", "info",
        "Login POST accepts forged Origin (mitigated by SameSite)",
        f["action"], method="POST",
        evidence="forged-origin login was accepted but session cookies carry "
                 "SameSite=Lax/Strict, which prevents browser-based CSRF",
        confidence="high", phase=2)]
F2 — check_logout_csrf
python
def check_logout_csrf(ctx):
    """F2 - logout CSRF: GET logout reachable from a forged Origin."""
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return []
    tester = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f:
        return []
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(tester, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return []
    home = tester.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    links, forms, _ = parse_page(home.text, home.url)
    logout_url, logout_method = None, "GET"
    for link in links:
        if re.search(r"(?i)logout|sign-out|signout|log-out", link):
            logout_url = link
            break
    if not logout_url:
        for form in forms:
            if re.search(r"(?i)logout|sign-out|signout", form["action"]):
                logout_url, logout_method = form["action"], "POST"
                break
    if not logout_url:
        return []

    forged = {"Origin": "https://wp-csrf-attacker.example",
              "Referer": "https://wp-csrf-attacker.example/"}
    before = tester.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    after = tester.fetch(logout_url, logout_method, headers=forged, follow=True)
    check = tester.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if after is None or check is None or anon is None:
        return []
    if similar(anon.text, check.text) > 0.9 and before is not None and \
            similar(anon.text, before.text) < 0.9:
        return [Finding(
            "logout-csrf", "low",
            f"Logout via {logout_method} works from a forged Origin",
            logout_url,
            evidence="session invalidated after a request with Origin/Referer "
                     "forged to wp-csrf-attacker.example",
            remediation="Require POST with a per-session CSRF token for logout, or "
                        "at minimum validate Origin/Referer.",
            phase=2)]
    return []
F3 — check_auth_change_csrf
python
def check_auth_change_csrf(ctx):
    """F3 - CSRF on password/email change forms."""
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    out = []
    candidates = [ctx.root + p for p in
                  ("/account/password", "/settings/password", "/profile/password",
                   "/account/security", "/settings/security",
                   "/account/email", "/settings/email", "/profile/email",
                   "/account/settings", "/settings/account")]
    home = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if home:
        for link in parse_page(home.text, home.url)[0]:
            if re.search(r"(?i)(password|email|account|profile|security|settings)", link):
                candidates.append(link)

    seen = set()
    for url in dict.fromkeys(candidates):
        page = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if page is None or page.status >= 400:
            continue
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        for f in forms:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            action = urllib.parse.urlsplit(f["action"]).path
            if action in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(action)
            fields = f["inputs"]
            is_pw = any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?pass|confirm.?pass|password1|newpassword)",
                                  k) for k in fields) and \
                    any(re.search(r"(?i)pass", k) for k in fields)
            is_email = any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?email|email)", k) for k in fields) and \
                       any(re.search(r"(?i)(new|change|update)", k) for k in fields)
            if not (is_pw or is_email):
                continue
            kind = "password change" if is_pw else "email change"
            has_token = any(CSRF_FIELD_RE.search(k) for k in fields)
            if not has_token:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "auth-change-csrf", "high",
                    f"{kind} form without anti-CSRF token",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence=f"fields: {', '.join(list(fields)[:8])}",
                    remediation="Require a per-session CSRF token, validated "
                                "server-side before any state change.",
                    phase=2))
            has_current = any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|existing)", k) for k in fields)
            if not has_current:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "auth-change-csrf", "high",
                    f"{kind} form does not require current password",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence="no current/old password field in the form",
                    remediation="Require the current password (and for email, "
                                "confirmation via the old address) before switching.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=2))
    return out
MFA — check_mfa_presence
python
def check_mfa_presence(ctx):
    _, outcome = _login_and_classify(ctx)
    if outcome == "no_form":
        return []
    if outcome == "no_creds":
        return [Finding("mfa", "info", "MFA presence not tested",
                        ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="--test-email/--test-password not set",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]
    if outcome == "mfa":
        return [Finding(
            "mfa", "info", "MFA challenge detected after login", ctx.base_url,
            evidence="post-login flow redirected to an MFA/OTP endpoint or served "
                     "an MFA/OTP form",
            remediation="E1 (bounded OTP guessing) and E3 (skip-MFA bypass) are "
                        "available via --otp-test; E2 (replay) and E4 (backup codes) "
                        "require the test inbox and are manual.",
            phase=2)]
    if outcome == "authed":
        return [Finding(
            "mfa", "medium", "No MFA challenge after successful password login",
            ctx.base_url,
            evidence="successful password login issued an authenticated session "
                     "without any MFA step",
            remediation="Require MFA on admin/staff; offer it to customers.",
            phase=2)]
    if outcome == "rejected":
        return [Finding("mfa", "info", "MFA presence undetermined (login rejected)",
                        ctx.base_url,
                        evidence="valid test credentials were rejected before any "
                                 "MFA step; verify --test-email/--test-password",
                        confidence="high", phase=2)]
    return []
E3 — check_mfa_bypass
python
def check_mfa_bypass(ctx):
    """E3 - skip MFA by direct navigation with the pre-MFA session."""
    c, outcome = _login_and_classify(ctx)
    if outcome != "mfa" or c is None:
        return []
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="").fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    anon_text = anon.text if anon else ""
    out = []
    targets = [ctx.root + p for p in
               ("/account", "/profile", "/dashboard", "/orders", "/bookings",
                "/settings", "/api/me", "/api/user", "/api/account")] + \
              [ctx.root + p for p in ADMIN_PATHS_P2[:6]]
    for url in targets:
        r = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status >= 400:
            continue
        if MFA_URL_RE.search(r.url) or MFA_URL_RE.search(r.header("Location")):
            continue
        if similar(anon_text, r.text) > 0.9:
            continue
        if re.search(r"(?i)(login|sign in|unauthorized|forbidden)", r.text[:2000]):
            continue
        out.append(Finding(
            "mfa", "high", f"MFA bypass: {url} accessible before verification",
            url,
            evidence=f"HTTP {r.status} with substantive body "
                     f"({clip(r.text[:160], 160)})",
            confidence="medium", phase=2))
        if len(out) >= 3:
            break
    return out
E1 — check_otp_bruteforce
python
def check_otp_bruteforce(ctx):
    """E1 - bounded OTP guessing (opt-in via --otp-test)."""
    if not ctx.args.otp_test:
        return []
    c, outcome = _login_and_classify(ctx)
    if outcome != "mfa" or c is None:
        return []
    home = c.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if not home:
        return []
    _, forms, _ = parse_page(home.text, home.url)
    otp_form = None
    for f in forms:
        if any(MFA_FIELD_RE.match(k) for k in f["inputs"]):
            otp_form = f
            break
    if not otp_form:
        return []
    n = min(ctx.args.rate_count, 12)
    codes = ["000000", "111111", "123456", "654321", "999999",
             "0000", "1111", "1234", "00000000", "12345678"]
    statuses, elapsed = [], 0.0
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    for i in range(n):
        params = dict(otp_form["inputs"])
        for k in params:
            if MFA_FIELD_RE.match(k):
                params[k] = codes[i % len(codes)]
        r = c.fetch(otp_form["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                    follow=True)
        if r is None:
            break
        statuses.append(r.status)
        if r.status == 429 or r.header("Retry-After"):
            break
    elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
    if len(statuses) >= n and not any(s in (429, 403, 503) for s in statuses):
        return [Finding(
            "mfa", "high", "No rate limit on OTP submissions",
            otp_form["action"], method="POST",
            evidence=f"{len(statuses)} OTP guesses in {elapsed:.1f}s without "
                     f"429/403/Retry-After",
            remediation="Throttle per session and per account; lock or terminate "
                        "the flow after 3–5 failures; require the user to restart MFA.",
            phase=2)]
    return []
Supabase — check_supabase
python
def _find_supabase_anon_key(pages):
    for page in pages:
        for m in re.finditer(r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\.eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}\."
                             r"[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{10,}", page.get("html", "")):
            dec = decode_jwt(m.group(0))
            if dec and dec[1].get("role") == "anon":
                return m.group(0)
    return None


def _supabase_login(sb_host, anon_key, email, password):
    probe = HttpClient()
    r = probe.fetch(sb_host.rstrip("/") + "/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password",
                    "POST",
                    json.dumps({"email": email, "password": password}),
                    headers={"apikey": anon_key,
                             "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    if r is None or r.status != 200:
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(r.text).get("access_token")
    except Exception:
        return None


def check_supabase(ctx):
    out = []
    # 1. access/refresh token in URL fragment
    for page in ctx.pages:
        html = page.get("html", "")
        if "#access_token=" in html or "#refresh_token=" in html:
            out.append(Finding(
                "supabase", "high",
                "Supabase access/refresh token in URL fragment",
                page["url"],
                evidence="response body contains '#access_token=' or "
                         "'#refresh_token='",
                remediation="Use the PKCE flow with a cookie-bound state; do not "
                            "use implicit-flow fragment tokens.",
                phase=2))
            break

    # 2. discover supabase.co hosts
    sb_hosts = set()
    for url in ctx.discovered + ctx.endpoints:
        m = re.search(r"https?://([a-z0-9\-]+)\.supabase\.co", url)
        if m:
            sb_hosts.add(m.group(0))
    if not sb_hosts:
        return out

    for host in list(sb_hosts)[:5]:
        # 3. unauthenticated schema disclosure
        probe = host.rstrip("/") + "/rest/v1/"
        r = ctx.http.fetch(probe, follow=True)
        if r is not None and r.status == 200 and \
                re.search(r"(?i)(\"paths\"|openapi|swagger)", r.text):
            out.append(Finding(
                "supabase", "high",
                "Supabase /rest/v1/ reachable unauthenticated",
                probe,
                evidence="HTTP 200 with OpenAPI/schema disclosure",
                remediation="Require the anon key at minimum; ensure every table "
                            "has RLS enabled so anonymous SELECT is denied.",
                phase=2))

        # 4. RLS probe with test token
        if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
            continue
        anon_key = _find_supabase_anon_key(ctx.pages)
        if not anon_key:
            continue
        access_token = _supabase_login(host, anon_key,
                                       ctx.args.test_email,
                                       ctx.args.test_password)
        if not access_token:
            continue
        schema = ctx.http.fetch(probe,
                                headers={"apikey": anon_key,
                                         "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
                                follow=True)
        if schema is None:
            continue
        tables = list(dict.fromkeys(
            re.findall(r"/rest/v1/([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", schema.text)))[:8]
        our_sub = None
        dec = decode_jwt(access_token)
        if dec:
            our_sub = dec[1].get("sub")
        for tbl in tables:
            url = host.rstrip("/") + f"/rest/v1/{tbl}?select=*&limit=5"
            rr = ctx.http.fetch(url,
                                headers={"apikey": anon_key,
                                         "Authorization": f"Bearer {access_token}"},
                                follow=True)
            if rr is None or rr.status != 200:
                continue
            try:
                rows = json.loads(rr.text)
            except Exception:
                continue
            if not isinstance(rows, list) or not rows:
                continue
            foreign = [row for row in rows
                       if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("user_id") and
                       our_sub and row["user_id"] != our_sub]
            if foreign:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "supabase", "critical",
                    f"RLS bypass on table '{tbl}'", url,
                    evidence=f"{len(rows)} rows returned; {len(foreign)} with a "
                             f"user_id outside the test account",
                    remediation="Enable RLS on every table with policies scoped "
                                "to auth.uid(); verify with SET ROLE authenticated.",
                    phase=2))
    return out
check_password_change
python
def check_password_change(ctx):
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    found_form, source_url = None, ""
    for url in [ctx.root + p for p in
                ("/account/password", "/settings/password", "/profile/password",
                 "/account/security", "/settings/security")]:
        page = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if page is None or page.status >= 400:
            continue
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        for f in forms:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            fields = f["inputs"]
            if any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?pass|confirm.?pass|password1|newpassword)", k)
                   for k in fields) and \
               any(re.search(r"(?i)pass", k) for k in fields):
                found_form, source_url = f, page["url"]
                break
        if found_form:
            break
    if not found_form:
        return []

    out = []
    fields = found_form["inputs"]
    has_current = any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|existing)", k) for k in fields)
    if not has_current:
        out.append(Finding(
            "password-change", "high",
            "Password change form does not require current password",
            found_form["action"], method="POST",
            evidence=f"fields: {', '.join(list(fields)[:8])}",
            remediation="Require the current password before accepting a new one.",
            phase=2))

    if not ctx.args.test_password_change:
        return out
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return out

    new_pass = ctx.args.test_password + "X" + rand_token("", 4)
    params = {}
    for k, v in fields.items():
        if re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|existing)", k):
            params[k] = ctx.args.test_password
        elif re.search(r"(?i)(new.?pass|password1|newpassword)", k):
            params[k] = new_pass
        elif re.search(r"(?i)confirm", k):
            params[k] = new_pass
        else:
            params[k] = v
    params = _refresh_csrf(c, source_url, found_form, params)
    r = c.fetch(found_form["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return out
    if re.search(r"(?i)(success|updated|changed|password set)", r.text[:2000]):
        out.append(Finding(
            "password-change", "info",
            "Password change succeeded without current password (destructive test)",
            found_form["action"], method="POST",
            evidence=f"account password changed to a synthetic value; old "
                     f"credential: {ctx.args.test_password!r}, new: {new_pass!r}",
            remediation="Restore the test account credential and require current "
                        "password on every change.",
            phase=2))
    return out
check_email_change
python
def check_email_change(ctx):
    c = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not c:
        return []
    out = []
    for url in [ctx.root + p for p in
                ("/account/email", "/settings/email", "/profile/email",
                 "/account/settings", "/settings/account")]:
        page = c.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if page is None or page.status >= 400:
            continue
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(page.text, page.url)
        for f in forms:
            if f["method"] != "POST":
                continue
            fields = f["inputs"]
            if not any(re.search(r"(?i)(new.?email|email)", k) for k in fields):
                continue
            if not any(re.search(r"(?i)(new|change|update)", k) for k in fields):
                continue
            needs = any(re.search(r"(?i)(current|old|password|verify|confirm)", k)
                        for k in fields)
            if not needs:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "email-change", "high",
                    "Email change form does not require current password",
                    f["action"], method="POST",
                    evidence=f"fields: {', '.join(list(fields)[:8])}",
                    remediation="Require the current password and confirm via the "
                                "old address before switching.",
                    phase=2))
            break
    return out

python
# =========================================================================== #
# PHASE 3 - extended injection checks
# =========================================================================== #

# A2 - UNION-based SQLi
def check_sqli_union(ctx, point):
    """A2 - UNION-based SQLi. Bounded column counting + marker reflection."""
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    base_len = len(base.body)
    marker = rand_token("wpu", 6)
    
    # Test comment syntax by trying an ORDER BY that would fail if comment works
    # First determine column count via ORDER BY (bounded to 15)
    cols = None
    for n in range(1, 16):
        for comment in ("-- -", "#", "/*"):
            payload = f"' ORDER BY {n}{comment}"
            r = point.send(ctx.http, payload)
            if r is None:
                continue
            # If ORDER BY n works but n+1 errors, we have n columns
            r_next = point.send(ctx.http, f"' ORDER BY {n+1}{comment}")
            if r_next is None:
                continue
            if r.status < 400 and (r_next.status >= 400 or 
                                   len(r_next.body) != len(r.body)):
                cols = n
                break
        if cols:
            break
    
    if not cols:
        return []
    
    # Now try UNION SELECT with marker in first column
    nulls = ", ".join(["NULL"] * cols)
    for comment in ("-- -", "#", "/*"):
        payload = f"' UNION SELECT {nulls}{comment}"
        # Replace first NULL with string marker
        parts = ["NULL"] * cols
        for i in range(cols):
            parts[i] = f"'{marker}'"
            p = f"' UNION SELECT {','.join(parts)}{comment}"
            r = point.send(ctx.http, p)
            if r is not None and marker in r.text:
                return [Finding(
                    "sqli", "high", "SQL injection (UNION-based)",
                    point.action, method=point.method, param=point.target,
                    payload=p,
                    evidence=f"marker '{marker}' reflected after determining "
                             f"{cols} columns",
                    remediation="Use parameterized queries; restrict DB "
                                "privileges so UNION remains unhelpful.",
                    phase=3)]
            parts[i] = "NULL"
    return []

# Multipart helper
def build_multipart(fields: dict, files: dict):
    """files = {name: (filename, content, mime)}"""
    boundary = "----wp" + rand_token("", 12)
    parts = []
    for name, value in fields.items():
        parts.append(f"--{boundary}\r\n"
                     f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"\r\n\r\n'
                     f"{value}\r\n")

                     f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"; '
                     f'filename="{filename}"\r\n'
                     f"Content-Type: {mime}\r\n\r\n")
        parts.append(content)
        parts.append("\r\n")
    parts.append(f"--{boundary}--\r\n")

python
def build_multipart(fields, files):
    boundary = "----wp" + rand_token("", 12)
    body = b""
    for name, value in fields.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode()
        body += f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"\r\n\r\n'.encode()
        body += str(value).encode() + b"\r\n"
    for name, (filename, content, mime) in files.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode()
        body += f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"; filename="{filename}"\r\n'.encode()
        body += f"Content-Type: {mime}\r\n\r\n".encode()
        body += content + b"\r\n"
    body += f"--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    return body, f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"

Let me write compact but complete code.

For the stored XSS / second-order SQLi, the pattern is:

Find a form that accepts text input and stores it (review, profile, contact, booking notes)

Submit a unique marker as that input

Find the view endpoint (usually the same page, or a list view like /reviews, /profile)

Check if the marker appears unencoded

For second-order SQLi, need to store a SQL payload and then trigger a query that uses that value. This is harder - usually requires the stored value to be used in a WHERE or concatenation. The heuristic:

Store ' in a field

Then find where that data is read back and used (e.g., a search that filters by the stored value)

If the read shows an error, it's second-order

Actually second-order is really hard to detect black-box reliably. Let me limit it to a "suspicion" check: store special chars, then trigger common views, look for SQL errors.

For DOM XSS static analysis:

Fetch JS bundles (Phase 1 already does this)

Search for innerHTML, document.write, eval, setTimeout with string arg

Search for location.hash, location.search, location.href as source

Report locations with potential flows

python
# =========================================================================== #
# PHASE 3 - extended injection
# =========================================================================== #

def _multipart(fields, files):
    boundary = "----wp" + rand_token("", 12)
    body = b""
    for name, value in fields.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode()
        body += f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"\r\n\r\n'.encode()
        body += str(value).encode() + b"\r\n"
    for name, (fname, content, mime) in files.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode()
        body += (f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"; '
                 f'filename="{fname}"\r\n').encode()
        body += f"Content-Type: {mime}\r\n\r\n".encode()
        body += content + b"\r\n"
    body += f"--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    return body, f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"


def _find_upload_forms(ctx):
    out = []
    for page in ctx.pages:
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if "multipart" in f.get("enctype", "") or \
               any(k.lower() in ("file", "upload", "image", "photo", "avatar", "document")
                   for k in f["inputs"]):
                out.append((page["url"], f))
    return out


# --- A2 UNION SQLi -----------------------------------------------------
def check_sqli_union(ctx, point):
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    marker = rand_token("wpu", 8)
    cols = None
    # Order-by column counting (bounded)
    for n in range(1, 12):
        for comment in ("-- -", "#"):
            p = f"' ORDER BY {n}{comment}"
            r = point.send(ctx.http, p)
            if r is None or r.status >= 500:
                continue
            p_next = f"' ORDER BY {n+1}{comment}"
            rn = point.send(ctx.http, p_next)
            if rn is None:
                continue
            if r.status < 400 and (rn.status >= 400 or
                                   abs(len(rn.body) - len(r.body)) > 30):
                cols = n
                break
        if cols:
            break
    if not cols:
        return []
    # Try UNION with marker at each position
    for comment in ("-- -", "#"):
        for i in range(cols):
            parts = ["NULL"] * cols
            parts[i] = f"'{marker}'"
            p = f"' UNION SELECT {','.join(parts)}{comment}"
            r = point.send(ctx.http, p)
            if r is not None and marker in r.text:
                return [Finding(
                    "sqli", "high", "SQL injection (UNION-based)",
                    point.action, point.method, point.target, p,
                    evidence=f"marker reflected via UNION at column {i+1} of {cols}",
                    remediation="Parameterize queries; restrict DB role privileges.",
                    phase=3)]
    return []


# --- A5 Stacked queries ------------------------------------------------
def check_sqli_stacked(ctx, point):
    if not ctx.args.time_based:
        return []
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None or base.elapsed > 2.0:
        return []
    for p in ("'; SELECT pg_sleep(5)-- -",
              "'; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- -",
              "'; SELECT SLEEP(5)-- -"):
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        r = point.send(ctx.http, p)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if time.monotonic() - t0 >= 4.5:
            return [Finding(
                "sqli", "critical", "SQL injection (stacked queries)",
                point.action, point.method, point.target, p,
                evidence=f"delay {time.monotonic()-t0:.1f}s",
                remediation="Disable multi-statement execution; parameterize.",
                phase=3)]
    return []


# --- B2/B3 NoSQL types + auth bypass ----------------------------------
def check_nosql_types(ctx, point):
    """Send arrays/objects where scalar expected; look for 500s or type errors."""
    if point.kind != "form":
        return []
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    tries = [
        ("array", f"{point.target}[]=wpa"),
        ("object", f"{point.target}[a]=wpb"),
        ("null", f"{point.target}=null"),
        ("bool", f"{point.target}=true"),
    ]
    for label, fragment in tries:
        url = point.action
        if point.method == "GET":
            sep = "&" if "?" in url else "?"
            r = ctx.http.fetch(url + sep + fragment, follow=False)
        else:
            # rebuild body with the raw fragment
            params = dict(point._refresh(ctx.http))
            body = urllib.parse.urlencode(params)
            r = ctx.http.fetch(point.action, "POST", body + "&" + fragment,
                              follow=False)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if r.status >= 500 and re.search(
                r"(?i)(typeerror|type error|cannot read|expected|cast|"
                r"validation|invalid type|array)", r.text):
            return [Finding(
                "nosql", "medium",
                f"Type confusion accepted ({label})",
                point.action, point.method, point.target, fragment,
                evidence=f"HTTP {r.status}: {clip(r.text, 160)}",
                remediation="Enforce schema validation; reject arrays/objects "
                            "where scalars are expected.",
                phase=3)]
    return []

Actually for stored XSS: plant XSS payload in a form, then re-visit the page and any views that display that data. If payload executes (or is reflected unencoded), it's stored XSS.

For second-order SQLi: harder. Plant special chars, then trigger a view. If SQL error appears, might be second-order.
